title: A Reinforcement Learning Method to Navigate SMEFT Operator Space
author: Jacky Kumar
contentSnippet:
Authors: Jacky Kumar

Abstract: In particle physics, discrepancies between experimental measurements and Standard Model (SM) predictions are commonly interpreted within new theoretical models. In this context, the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) provides a general framework encompassing a broad class of models. However, exploring the enormous space of possible SMEFT operators rapidly becomes a challenging combinatorial problem: many operators can contribute simultaneously to different observables, their effects are correlated, and distinct operator combinations can provide comparably good descriptions of the data. In this work, we formulate the exploration of the SMEFT operator space as a sequential decision-making problem using reinforcement learning (RL). Our RL agent employs a lightweight actor-critic architecture with approximately 40K trainable parameters in total. Rather than searching for a single best-fit theory, our method is designed to discover a diverse set of high-quality theory hypotheses. We test the method in a complex phenomenological environment comprising 132 observables across several sectors of particle physics, including 24 measurements that deviate from their SM predictions by more than $1.5\sigma$. We show that the learned RL policy efficiently constructs multi-operator theories that substantially improve the global fit. Comparisons with independent random-subset and random-sequential searches demonstrate the ability of the RL policy to navigate this large combinatorial space. Our results establish RL as a systematic framework for exploring diverse patterns of new physics (NP) interactions within SMEFT.

Notes: 15 pages, 3 figures, GitHub Link: this https URL

summary.tldr:
Jacky Kumar introduces a reinforcement learning (RL) framework to navigate the Standard Model Effective Field Theory (SMEFT) operator space, addressing the combinatorial complexity of identifying new physics interactions. By framing the selection of SMEFT operators as a sequential decision-making problem, the approach moves beyond traditional best-fit searches to identify a diverse set of high-quality theoretical hypotheses that explain experimental discrepancies.

The RL agent utilizes a lightweight actor-critic architecture containing approximately 40,000 trainable parameters. The model was evaluated against a phenomenological dataset consisting of 132 observables, including 24 measurements that deviate from Standard Model predictions by more than 1.5σ. The RL policy demonstrated superior efficiency in constructing multi-operator theories compared to random-subset and random-sequential search baselines, effectively managing the correlations between operators and their collective impact on global fit metrics.
takeaways: **Architecture:** The RL agent uses an actor-critic model with ~40K trainable parameters.
**Dataset Scope:** The framework was tested on 132 distinct particle physics observables.
**Performance Metric:** The model successfully identified multi-operator theories that improve global fits, specifically addressing 24 measurements with >1.5σ deviations.
**Methodological Advantage:** The RL approach outperformed random-subset and random-sequential search strategies in navigating the combinatorial SMEFT operator space.

title: Sage S2.1 Flash Technical Report
author: Kun Cai, Haodong Chen, Guangran Cheng, Qingxiu Cheng
contentSnippet:
Abstract: We introduce Sage S1.5 Flash, a 320-billion-parameter general-purpose mixture-of-experts model designed to reason over scientific evidence and act in interactive environments. Sage Sci-Perception uses dedicated encoders for molecular graphs and biological sequences and represents spectra as ordered patches of measurements. Modality-specific projectors map these representations into the input space of a shared backbone, which processes them alongside text and images. To develop the model's agent capabilities, we construct verifiable environments for tool use, search, and coding, as well as specialized workflows involving machine learning experiments and scientific software. Task completion is checked against execution results, changes in environment state, or submitted artifacts. We evaluate Sage S1.5 Flash on 33 benchmarks across seven domains. In the primary comparison against five baselines, it ranks first on OfficeQA Pro (72.2), MLE-bench Lite (90.3 HumanRank), Harvey LAB, and SpreadsheetBench~2, and second on OSWorld-Verified (85.2), WebArena-Verified (67.6), and DeepResearch Bench~II (54.2). These results show particular strengths in using documentary evidence, producing verifiable workbooks, and carrying out machine learning tasks, alongside competitive performance in desktop and browser workflows that require the model to act on visual feedback.

Notes: website: this https URL

summary.tldr:
Sage S1.5 Flash is a 320-billion-parameter mixture-of-experts (MoE) model engineered for scientific reasoning and interactive agentic tasks. Developed to bridge the gap between multimodal perception and environment-based execution, the model integrates specialized encoders for molecular graphs, biological sequences, and spectral data, mapping these inputs into a shared backbone alongside standard text and image processing capabilities.

To optimize agentic performance, the researchers built verifiable environments for tool use, coding, and machine learning experimentation, where task success is validated through execution results and state changes. In testing across 33 benchmarks, Sage S1.5 Flash achieved top-tier performance, ranking first on OfficeQA Pro (72.2), MLE-bench Lite (90.3 HumanRank), Harvey LAB, and SpreadsheetBench~2. It secured second place on OSWorld-Verified (85.2), WebArena-Verified (67.6), and DeepResearch Bench~II (54.2), demonstrating high proficiency in documentary evidence analysis and automated scientific workflows.

**Top Benchmark Performance:** Ranked first on OfficeQA Pro (72.2) and MLE-bench Lite (90.3 HumanRank).
**Agentic Capabilities:** Evaluated on 33 benchmarks across seven domains, focusing on verifiable tool use, search, coding, and machine learning experiment execution.
**Competitive Standing:** Achieved second-place rankings on OSWorld-Verified (85.2), WebArena-Verified (67.6), and DeepResearch Bench~II (54.2).

title: InclusionMed: Benchmarking AI for Inclusive Healthcare
author: The InclusionMed Collaboration
contentSnippet: Advancing medical AI for inclusive healthcare requires evaluation across diverse healthcare roles, tasks, and care settings, but benchmark coverage remains uneven. We introduce InclusionMed, an open medical AI evaluation initiative for inclusive healthcare. The InclusionMed Atlas organizes benchmarks across three healthcare roles and three AI capabilities. For the first release, we selected four public benchmarks from 388 candidates through structured audits and independent reproduction. With InclusionMed-DxFiles, our private diagnostic reasoning benchmark, the Atlas contains five benchmarks covering three of its nine role--capability cells. We evaluated frontier large language models on the Atlas and aggregated their results into the InclusionMed Index, with overall scores ranging from 17.5 to 49.1 out of 100. The Index also reports scores by healthcare role and AI capability, showing that a model's rank varied with the role or capability considered. A within-benchmark analysis using task-level tags showed that the ten highest-ranked models in the Index all scored higher on patient communication than on clinical decision-making. Models with similar Index scores also differed substantially in estimated inference cost. These findings highlight the need for evaluation covering more diverse healthcare needs and for context-specific model selection. Through open collaboration and community contributions, InclusionMed seeks to ensure that diverse healthcare needs worldwide shape how medical AI progress is defined and measured.

title: DominoBench: Evaluating Multi-Step Physical Reasoning from Still Images
author: Emilio Ferrara
contentSnippet: Can a vision-language model look at a picture of a chain reaction and tell what will happen? Recent multimodal models describe scenes fluently and solve textbook physics problems, which suggests they should also predict how a scene of ramps, ledges, pendulums, seesaws and dominoes plays out once a ball is pushed. We tested this claim on 30 models from 10 families and reached a clear conclusion: unaided, no model predicts the outcome reliably. We built DominoBench, a benchmark of still images of 2D rigid-body scenes whose outcome a physics simulator computes. It holds 854 items in 427 minimal pairs, in which a change of one to three grid steps in one quantity decides whether one person survives, and every item comes with a four-rung hint ladder ending in the exact calculation that decides the outcome. Unaided, frontier models from Anthropic, Google and OpenAI are right about the person whose fate flips in at most 72% of items and answer both twins of a pair correctly in at most 34%. Pointing at the deciding step helps little, and exact geometry given as text barely helps, yet once the deciding calculation and the quantities it needs, including speeds that a still image cannot show, are written out, the same models reach 82-92% on the deciding person, while small open-weight models stay near chance. Physical prediction from a still image therefore fails at the quantitative step: the strongest models use the deciding quantity when they are given it, but do not produce it on their own. For models that plan or act in the physical world, a fluent account of a scene is thus no evidence of a correct prediction: such models must find and compute the deciding quantity unprompted, and DominoBench tests whether they do.

title: Accelerate Bench: Evaluating Agents for Application-Level Program Optimization
author: Bowen Liu, Yuhan Li, Nuo Chen, Weile Luo
contentSnippet: Application optimization requires coding agents to discover useful changes and coordinate them across a complete program while preserving the required computation. We introduce Accelerate Bench, a benchmark of 32 CPU optimization tasks adapted from scientific applications and supercomputing competitions. Each task provides a working program and specifies the workload, correctness requirements, timing boundaries, and permitted edits, leaving agents to choose where and how to optimize. Public testing supports iterative development, and a separate verifier scores the final submission. On benchmark version 1.1, we evaluate 16 coding agents, each pairing a model with a harness. Their Score@1 ranges from 25.5% to 67.4%. Most of their programs are correct, and the size of the speedup separates them: the two leading agents are at least 2x faster on 22 or more of the 32 tasks, while the other fourteen reach 2x on 8 to 17 and leave 125 of their 412 correct outcomes below 1.25x. Controlled replays show why coordination across an application matters: identical source code runs between 0.29x and 2.12x depending only on build and runtime settings, and one code change is worth 1.01x or 6.4x depending on another. Accelerate Bench pairs executable workloads with agents' programs and trajectories to evaluate both their gains and the process behind them.

title: ScaleVLA: Scaling Vision-Language-Action Models to 552 Billion Parameters
author: Ruixi Yu, Dairu Liu, Xuchuan Chen, Zekun Qi
contentSnippet: Frontier Vision-Language Models (VLMs) such as GPT-6 Astra have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in robot control, suggesting that broad pretraining provides knowledge valuable for physical action. Yet most Vision-Language-Action (VLA) policies still rely on much smaller VLM backbones, leaving this potential largely untapped. We ask whether frontier-scale representations can provide a stronger foundation for robot learning. We introduce ScaleVLA, which connects a 552B DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash backbone to a trainable action DiT, and systematically compare VLMs from 2B to 552B under a shared training setup. We evaluate three fundamental capabilities of robot foundation models. In sample efficiency, just 10 demonstrations outperform a 2B backbone trained with 50 (87.8% vs. 85.6%). In generalization, LIBERO-PRO success reaches 45.1%, compared with at most 31.3% for smaller backbones. In precise manipulation, real-world charger insertion improves from 4/10 to 9/10 successes, with gains concentrated in contact-sensitive alignment. Despite its scale, ScaleVLA achieves 216 ms median latency per action chunk. Our findings suggest that frontier VLMs can serve not only as reasoning agents, but also as powerful representational foundations for efficient and generalizable robot policies.

title: MovieRoll: A Systematic Framework for Rolling Out Long-Form Videos
author: Yunyang Ge, Weijie Kong, Ryan Xu, Yue Wu
contentSnippet: Streaming video generation must sustain quality beyond the training horizon while handling self-generated history and growing cache costs. To address these challenges, we present MovieRoll, a base-to-distilled framework that connects streaming fine-tuning, long-rollout distillation, and long-horizon inference. We first establish a robust multi-step base through Window-wise Teacher Forcing (WinTF), which jointly denoises chunks at progressive noise levels with bidirectional attention within each window and causal access to preceding history. To retain historical context efficiently, hierarchical KV-cache compression (HieraKV) exploits layer-wise attention patterns, retaining full history in shallow layers and sink--recent history in deeper layers. This reduces cache memory by up to 78% while improving generation quality. Building on this base, cumulative long tuning with distribution matching distillation (CuLT-DMD) holds parameters fixed throughout each long self-rollout and averages local gradients before updating. Each update therefore combines supervision across temporal positions while retaining only one local computation graph, enabling efficient long-rollout training of a few-step generator. To extend generation beyond the training horizon, KV recomputation bounds context for both models, while guidance annealing (AnnealCFG) reduces guidance toward the clean endpoint to stabilize MovieRoll-Base. Complementing these modeling advances, FBCA attention and PS-VAE decoding support efficient training and streaming output. On HeliosBench, MovieRoll-Base remains competitive at 30s after training on videos of up to 15s, and MovieRoll-Distilled achieves the highest total scores among the compared methods across single- and multi-event evaluations up to 60s, combining sustained naturalness with active motion.

title: K2-Horizon: A Frontier Fleet of Open Source Language Models
author: K2 Team, Zhengzhong Liu, Haonan Li, Xuezhe Ma
contentSnippet: We present K2-Horizon, a fleet of six fully open language models, from a 0.9B dense model to a 375B-A23B MoE, built for general-purpose reasoning and agentic work across math and science, software engineering, deep research, office automation, and beyond. The models lead or are competitive with strong open models of their size on agentic and coding benchmarks. On the modeling side, to strengthen reasoning, we introduce Mixture-of-Value Attention (MoVA), applying MoE to attention value projections, and softplus attention gating, a more flexible, theoretically motivated gate. Our 36B-A4B model uses both and nearly matches a 32B dense model trained on the same data, with one-seventh the active parameters. We also introduce Uno, lossless diffusion adapters that speed up decoding by up to 2.2x without a separate draft model. Our release follows the LLM360 definition of open source for transparency and reproducibility: the full development history, including intermediate checkpoints from every training stage, pre-training data, training logs, and all training, evaluation, and infrastructure code, notably our production-scale xLLM framework for dense and MoE training and the RL360 reinforcement-learning stack. Beyond the data itself, we release and document in detail every pipeline that built it, the part of model development that open releases most rarely disclose. These pipelines produced roughly 10T synthetic pre-training tokens, showing that synthetic data can be a major ingredient of pre-training at scale. Four of the models share one 22T-token pre-training corpus and recipe, revealing consistent scaling behavior and enabling controlled studies of scale and sparsity. All artifacts are available at https://ifm.ai/k2/

title: datasette-maplibre 0.1a0
author: Simon Willison AI
contentSnippet:
15th November 2026 Release datasette-maplibre 0.1a0 — Visualize geospatial data in Datasette using MapLibre GL and OpenFreeMap The first new Datasette geospatial plugin in quite a while! This one combines the excellent MapLibre GL library with OpenFreeMap , the free vector map server operated by Zsolt Ero (you should sponsor Zsolt on GitHub .)

I built most of this with a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2:

Look at datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson plugins, then look at ~/dev/tools/openfreemap-demo.html - then build a brand new Datasette plugin that uses maplibreGL and openfreemap and combines the features of those other two plugins - but be creative and think outside the box for other useful features the plugin might have

"Be creative and think outside the box" resulted in a few neat ideas - my favorite is that it displays SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes, then loads a WebGL preview only when they scroll into view.

I also had Claude build a comprehensive demo which works in the latest Datasette Lite, so you can visit this link to load the plugin and a demo database in your browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly.

I like this demo page showing both GeoJSON shapes and lat/lon points on the same map:

summary.tldr:
Simon Willison has released datasette-maplibre 0.1a0, a new geospatial plugin for the Datasette ecosystem that integrates MapLibre GL with the OpenFreeMap vector map server. The plugin is designed to consolidate functionality from existing tools like datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson, providing a unified interface for visualizing both GeoJSON shapes and latitude/longitude coordinate points on a single map.

Developed primarily using Claude Fable 5.2, the plugin features an optimization for performance: it renders SVG previews of GeoJSON shapes initially, deferring the loading of the resource-intensive WebGL preview until the user scrolls the element into view. The project is fully compatible with Datasette Lite, allowing users to run the plugin and interact with demo databases directly in the browser via Pyodide and WebAssembly.
takeaways: **Plugin Architecture:** Combines MapLibre GL for rendering with OpenFreeMap as the vector map provider.
**Performance Optimization:** Implements lazy-loading for WebGL map previews by using SVG placeholders for GeoJSON shapes until they enter the viewport.
**Development Methodology:** Built using a single prompt to Claude Fable 5.2, referencing existing codebase patterns from datasette-cluster-map and datasette-leaflet-geojson.

title: Indian chip startup Bharat Semi lands $24M seed round as it eyes global AI sensor market
author: Jagmeet Singh
contentSnippet: Bharat Semi says it has secured design wins for its AI-enabled sensor technology with companies, including General Atomics.

summary.tldr:
New Delhi-based semiconductor startup Bharat Semi has secured $24 million in an all-equity seed funding round led by Info Edge Group, South Park Commons, and Indus Bridge Ventures. The company, founded in 2021 by Vrinda Kapoor and Vinayak Dalmia, is developing programmable image sensors that integrate image capture, processing, and AI capabilities onto a single chip. By eliminating the need for separate image signal processors and system-on-chips, the startup claims its architecture can reduce system costs by at least 70% for applications in smart homes, industrial automation, surveillance, and aerospace.

Bharat Semi currently operates as a fabless entity with 75 employees, including a small engineering and business development team in Santa Clara, California. The company has secured design wins with General Atomics and Kaynes Semicon, though its products remain in the prototyping phase. The first generation of sensors is currently being prototyped, with second-generation sensors featuring advanced AI capabilities expected to reach the prototype stage by mid-2027, followed by commercial availability by the end of that year. The startup intends to use the new capital to scale its engineering team and finalize product development, with plans to grow its U.S. headcount to approximately 20 by 2027.

**Operational Footprint:** Employs 75 people across India and the U.S., with plans to expand the Santa Clara office to 20 employees and initiate hiring in Europe.

title: datasette 1.0a43
author: Simon Willison AI
contentSnippet: Release: datasette 1.0a43 I've been leaning hard into Claude Fable 5.2 to help knock things off the 1.0 milestone , which is now 53% complete. The biggest 1.0 item in this release is streaming support for output renderers - the built-in TSV and CSV export mechanisms now use this as well, and plugins can register themselves as capable of streaming every row in a table in one go via the new Response.stream() method. There are a couple of security fixes, one of which I deemed deserving of a GitHub advisory : private stored queries could be exposed, granting access to the title and SQL of the query (but not allowing that query to be executed). There are dozens of smaller improvements. The row page JSON representation finally has a design suitable for 1.0 . A new <datasette-copy-button> Web Component provides copy-schema in various places. JSON in columns on the row page can be pretty-printed. There's a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JavaScript utility method. Plus dozens of bug fixes, including contributions by Zihan Dai , Peter Olkhovets , Ilya Khalafi , and Ankita Advitot . The feature I'm most excited about is a pretty tiny one: I've added CSS multi-page view transitions to Datasette! Here's the commit - key CSS is as follows: /* Enable cross-document view transitions, for anyone without prefers-reduced-motion */ @media ( prefers-reduced-motion : no-preference ) { @view-transition { navigation : auto ; } } /* .facet-results should morph from old position to new */ html : active-view-transition . content > . facet-results { view-transition-name : facet-results ; } /* So should a .table-wrapper, provided it contains .rows-and-columns */ html : active-view-transition . table-wrapper : has ( > table . rows-and-columns ) { view-transition-name : rows-table ; } With that in place, navigations within Datasette - still staunchly a multi-page application - feel more like an SPA. This works on Safari and Chrome at the moment and I believe supports for Firefox is due to land in Firefox 162 on December 8th 2026 (seeing as they are no longer feature-flagged in Firefox Nightly.) Tags: security , datasette , css , browsers , annotated-release-notes , firefox , javascript , safari , chrome

summary.tldr:
Datasette 1.0a43 has been released, marking the project as 53% complete toward its 1.0 milestone. The update introduces streaming support for output renderers, allowing built-in TSV and CSV exports to stream data, and provides a new Response.stream() method for plugin developers to stream entire table rows in a single operation. The release also addresses a security vulnerability, documented in a GitHub advisory, where private stored queries could have their titles and SQL exposed to unauthorized users, though the queries themselves remained unexecutable.

Technical enhancements include a finalized JSON representation for row pages, a new Web Component for schema copying, and a JavaScript utility, DatasetteModal.confirm(). The release also integrates CSS multi-page view transitions, enabling SPA-like navigation behavior within the multi-page application framework. This feature is currently supported in Safari and Chrome, with Firefox support expected in version 162, scheduled for release on December 8, 2026. The update includes numerous bug fixes contributed by Zihan Dai, Peter Olkhovets, Ilya Khalafi, and Ankita Advitot.
takeaways: **Milestone Progress:** The Datasette 1.0 release is now 53% complete, with development assisted by Claude Fable 5.2.
**Streaming Architecture:** New Response.stream() method allows plugins to stream full table rows, now utilized by default TSV and CSV export mechanisms.
**Security Fix:** A GitHub advisory was issued for a vulnerability that allowed the exposure of private stored query titles and SQL definitions.
**UI/UX Improvements:** Added CSS multi-page view transitions to mimic SPA navigation, alongside pretty-printing for JSON columns and a new DatasetteModal.confirm() JS utility.
**Browser Compatibility:** View transitions are active in Safari and Chrome, with Firefox 162 support slated for December 8, 2026.

title: Is bad news for Jensen Huang also bad news for the AI industry?
author: Anthony Ha

We didn’t see this coming. Or at least, I didn’t — a week ago, when I wrote about Nvidia’s board opening an investigation into then-CEO Jensen Huang, I assumed his job was safe.

On the latest episode of TechCrunch’s Equity podcast , Rebecca Bellan, Tim De Chant, and I discussed how Huang’s ouster went down and what it means for the larger AI economy. While Tim said he saw it coming (albeit not this quickly), Rebecca said, “I didn’t think it was going to happen at all.”

“Jensen is Nvidia, right?” she added. “And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia.”

Similarly, I marveled at how quickly Huang’s support seemed to crumble, with more scandals seeming to emerge every day. (At the same time, there are many who’d still like to see him return .) And we also took a moment to wonder what will happen to Nvidia’s investments in the larger AI ecosystem.

Keep reading for a preview of our conversation, edited for length and clarity; you can listen to the whole episode here .

Rebecca Bellan: I didn’t think it was going to happen at all. I mean, Jensen is Nvidia, right? And so much of this economy is riding on Nvidia. And we’ve got nothing but the last few years of data to show us that billionaires can do whatever the hell they want. So it was surprising to me — it almost restored my faith in humanity, that he resigned.

But someone said to me, “If this were Elon, nothing would happen.” He would not be resigning. Nothing would be going down

Anthony Ha: Which is interesting, because I would have said, as of a week ago, or even just a few days ago, that Jensen is in the same category as Elon. But for those who somehow don

summary.tldr:
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following a series of scandals, including an admitted affair with an executive at a customer firm, Megaspeed, which allegedly has ties to Chinese intelligence. The resignation follows a rapid collapse of board support after reports surfaced regarding his personal conduct and potential national security implications. Nvidia CFO Collette Kress has been appointed as interim CEO, a move interpreted by analysts as a caretaker measure focused on expense management rather than long-term strategic leadership.

The fallout centers on concerns regarding Huang’s advocacy for loosening chip export restrictions to China, which critics argue prioritized sales over national security. Intelligence reports regarding Huang’s relationship with an individual linked to Chinese intelligence had reportedly been circulating for nearly a year. The situation reached a breaking point following a Bloomberg report on November 9, which alleged that Nvidia’s head attorney inquired about a Department of Commerce investigation into the matter, signaling to the board and government officials that the issue extended beyond personal misconduct into potential corporate interference.

Nvidia’s current market position is critical to the broader AI economy, as the company controls approximately 80% of the AI GPU market. The firm holds $99 billion in investments, $25 billion in commitments, and $36 billion in cloud service commitments, with significant stakes in major AI entities including OpenAI, Anthropic, CoreWeave, and Nebius. Analysts are now questioning the future of Nvidia’s aggressive investment strategy and its role as the primary infrastructure provider for the global AI ecosystem.

**Escalation Timeline:** The situation accelerated significantly following a November 9 Bloomberg report detailing the involvement of Nvidia’s legal counsel in inquiries regarding a Department of Commerce investigation.

title: Microfitting: Continual Learning via Cached Test-Time Training
author: Nick Ryan
contentSnippet: Continual learning is a promising approach to specialize language models to an organization's private data. However, current methods exhibit a number of drawbacks including catastrophic forgetting, where new training updates overwrite prior knowledge. We present microfitting, which trains and caches a small adapter for each document. Each adapter is trained once, offline, on synthetic questions targeted at demonstrated base-model shortcomings and reused whenever that document is queried. This method borrows from test-time learning literature and sidesteps the problem of continual learning through parameter isolation, allowing the system to specialize on new data without overwriting prior knowledge. The process that generates adapter training data also improves over time, revising its recipe from previous outcomes and fresh examples of the target workload. On DeepSeek V4 Flash, microfitting substantially improves accuracy over the base model. In Enterprise Document Operations (EDO), an open-book Q&A environment over real-world enterprise documents, our method achieves a 38.2% relative improvement over base-model performance. Microfitting makes continual specialization practical and cost-efficient: a frozen model can adapt to an evolving private corpus overnight on local hardware, without modifying the base model or previously cached adapters.

title: Jensen Huang might be plotting a return and more of the latest Nvidia drama
author: Terrence O’Brien
contentSnippet: The drama around Nvidia co-founder and former CEO Jensen Huang is evolving quickly. The latest edition of our Stepback newsletter should get you up to speed, but there have already been a number of new developments since this morning. That includes rumors that Jensen Huang might be trying to find a path back to CEO, and a statement from Megaspeed claiming that Alice Huang hasn’t worked for the company since August of 2025, which raises more questions than it answers. * Some big names, including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, have publicly thrown their support behind a public letter demanding Nvidia “bring Jensen back.” * The public letter calling for Jensen Huang to be reinstated has over 150,000 signatures, but it’s difficult to verify their authenticity. Business Insider reports that signatures include “Tim Cruise, Hollywood actor” and “Xi Jingping,” likely a misspelling of Chinese president Xi Jinping. * The Financial Times reports that Jensen Huang has discussed the possibility of returning as CEO with close allies, as some Silicon Valley insiders and employees attempt to pressure the board. * Not all believe Jensen Huang should be allowed to return to his seat. According to the Financial Times, one ally acknowledged that, “Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offense.” * 23andMe founder Anne Wojcicki told Bloomberg that “Power corrupts, and people start to think they are invincible … We are all complicit in making these people think they are gods. And people do stupid things when they think they are untouchable.” * Wojcicki endured a messy public divorce from Google co-founder Sergey Brin, after it was revealed he was having an affair with an employee. * According to Bloomberg, many women in Silicon Valley see Jensen Huang as simply another example of a rich man abusing their position and “leveraging power to pursue sexual relationships with their employees.” * Megaspeed released a statement saying that Alice Huang left the company “effective Aug. 30, 2025, and currently has no role with the company,” adding that “Megaspeed does not comment on Ms. Huang’s personal and private matters.”

summary.tldr:
Nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang is reportedly exploring a return to the CEO position amid internal and external pressure, according to reports from the Financial Times. This movement is supported by a public letter demanding his reinstatement, which has garnered over 150,000 signatures, though the authenticity of these signatures has been questioned due to the inclusion of names like 'Tim Cruise' and 'Xi Jingping.' High-profile figures including Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have publicly backed the campaign for his return.

Controversy persists regarding the circumstances of his departure, specifically allegations of an affair with a subordinate, which allies acknowledge is a fireable offense. Simultaneously, the company Megaspeed issued a statement clarifying that Alice Huang has held no role at the firm since August 30, 2025, declining further comment on her private matters. The situation has drawn broader criticism from Silicon Valley figures like 23andMe founder Anne Wojcicki, who characterized the behavior as a recurring pattern of powerful executives abusing their positions.
takeaways: **Public Support:** Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney have publicly endorsed the campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO.

**Petition Integrity:** The public letter demanding Huang's return claims over 150,000 signatures, though reports indicate the list includes clearly falsified entries such as 'Tim Cruise' and 'Xi Jingping'.
**Employment Status:** Megaspeed officially stated that Alice Huang ceased all roles with the company effective August 30, 2025.
**Ethical Criticism:** 23andMe founder Anne Wojcicki publicly criticized the culture of executive entitlement, citing the incident as an example of leaders believing they are 'untouchable'.

title: Congress wants to tighten export rules on AI chips after Nvidia spy scandal
author: Terrence O’Brien
contentSnippet: Unsurprisingly, following the scandal involving now-former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and a suspected Chinese spy, Congress is looking to further restrict exports of AI chips. Both Democrats and Republicans have voiced support for various measures and bills that would tighten rules and have demanded that Huang and other Nvidia leaders testify before Congress. Senate Minority Leader Chuck Schumer has already said that Huang and the Trump administration need to answer to Congress. Senate Banking Committee Chairman Tim Scott has also sent letters to both Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick calling on them to publicly testify to the committee. Bills such as the Remote Access Security Act, first introduced in the House in April 2025 but stalled in the Senate, are receiving renewed interest. While that specific bill might not become law, House Speaker Mike Johnson has said there is “growing consensus in Congress on limiting chip exports to China,” according to Reuters. Johnson has also said that he personally supports efforts to restrict China’s access to powerful AI chips from companies like Nvidia.

title: An overview of Jensen Huang’s messy days
author: Terrence O’Brien
contentSnippet: This is The Stepback, a weekly newsletter breaking down one essential story from the tech world. For more on Jensen Huang’s resignation and the fallout from Nvidia’s leadership crisis, follow Terrence O’Brien. The Stepback arrives in our subscribers’ inboxes on Sunday at 8AM ET. Opt in for The Stepback here. How it started On October 29th, The New York Times reported that Nvidia co-founder and showman CEO Jensen Huang appeared to be the target of a Chinese spy plot. Any major tech CEO potentially being compromised by the Chinese government is concerning — especially Jensen Huang. “If you could draw the network diagram of the entire US AI ecosystem, Nvidia would be at the center of that,” Kyle Chan, a foreign policy fellow at the Brookings Institution’s John L. Thornton China Center, previously told The Verge. “If you could draw the diagram of the entire Nvidia ecosystem, a single man is standing at the heart of all of that.” The Times reported that Jensen Huang had developed a “close relationship” with Alice Huang (no relation), an executive at Singapore-based data center company Megaspeed. Alice Huang had been on the American government’s radar for some time, perhaps as early as 2024. Her company was investigated by the US Commerce Department over suspicions it was illegally smuggling Nvidia’s AI chips into China in violation of US government trade restrictions. Singapore authorities confiscated her passport back in June of 2025, eventually barring her from the country, after she reportedly gave “inaccurate information” to police. And perhaps more concerningly, some US officials believed she was passing information, possibly about Nvidia’s designs or the White House’s deliberations over trade restrictions, directly back to Beijing. This made her relationship with Jensen Huang concerning for multiple reasons. Nvidia’s chips are considered crucial to America’s AI superiority and a matter of national security by the White House. The government has restricted the sale of Nvidia’s most advanced chips to China since the Biden administration. But Jensen Huang has routinely pushed to loosen those trade restrictions. Meanwhile, he had gotten quite cozy with President Trump, once even putting him on speakerphone on-stage at the All-In Summit. Then last week, things escalated quickly. On Friday, November 6th, the Times reported that Alice Huang was specifically recrui

summary.tldr:
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following a series of scandals involving extramarital affairs and alleged national security compromises. The crisis began in late October 2025 when reports emerged that Huang had a relationship with Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed—a firm under US Commerce Department investigation for allegedly smuggling Nvidia chips into China. Following reports that Alice Huang was recruited by China’s Ministry of State Security to spy on him, Jensen Huang admitted to an affair on November 8th. The situation deteriorated further on November 11th when reports surfaced of a second affair with an internal direct report, Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s VP of Healthcare. By November 12th, Huang resigned, with CFO Colette Kress appointed as interim CEO and Harvey Jones named the company’s first-ever board chair.

The leadership transition has triggered significant market volatility, with Nvidia’s stock price falling from an all-time high of $239.24 on October 6th to $162.85 by November 13th. The company, which has invested $99 billion in AI infrastructure and announced plans for $500 billion in data center financing, now faces an ongoing board investigation and potential congressional scrutiny. Analysts suggest the company may undergo a major structural reorganization, as the board seeks to address the unusual management model where Huang maintained approximately 60 direct reports. Further complications include a shareholder lawsuit and potential civil or criminal liability regarding the company's compliance with US export restrictions to China, following allegations that Nvidia misled investors about its China-based revenue.
takeaways: **Leadership Changes:** Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, and Harvey Jones has been appointed as Nvidia's first board chair to oversee the search for a permanent successor.
**Market Impact:** Nvidia stock dropped from a peak of $239.24 on October 6th to $162.85 on November 13th following the resignation.
**Corporate Governance:** The board is expected to overhaul Nvidia’s management structure, specifically addressing the previous CEO's practice of maintaining 60 direct reports.

**Regulatory Exposure:** Nvidia faces potential congressional investigations and legal risks regarding the alleged smuggling of chips to China via Megaspeed and discrepancies in reported China-based revenue.

title: Bland Launches Tofu-1, a Full-Duplex Speech-to-Speech Model for Calls
author: Michal Sutter
contentSnippet: Bland, the San Francisco voice-AI company, has released Tofu-1 , a full-duplex speech-to-speech model in research preview. The Tofu-1 speech-to-speech model targets calls from moving cars, hospital rooms and weak-signal lines. It listens while it speaks and reasons while it talks. For phone-agent teams, one model now handles audio in and audio out, with no transcript between. You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension . What is Tofu-1? Tofu-1 is a full-duplex speech-to-speech model from Bland that hears, reasons and replies in audio during phone calls. It is the first release in a planned family of Bland speech-to-speech models. How does Tofu-1 differ from a cascade voice agent? Most voice agents are cascades. They turn speech into text, pass it to a language model, then turn the reply back into speech. Tofu-1 listens to the audio directly , so tone, hesitation and background sound stay available to the model. Bland has not published the internal architecture. Audio understanding Bland lists 3 audio skills on its product page: Speaker tracking: tells speakers apart and works out who each one is addressing. Noise separation: separates voices from a crying child, a TV, highway traffic, a hospital intercom or keypad tones. Paralinguistics: hears hesitation, frustration and urgency. Full duplex and thinking while talking Callers can interrupt or correct Tofu-1 mid-sentence. While it works on a request, it keeps the conversation moving. It reports the result only when the work is done. It never claims a task is finished early. Scene generation Because Tofu-1 models the sound of a call, it can also produce one. That includes a second speaker, the room around them and line noise. What is Bland’s ‘TV Test’? The TV Test asks one question: can the model follow the caller while ignoring speech from another scene? TV audio is often louder than the caller. Bland marks its TV Test walkthrough as illustrative, not recorded model output. How does Tofu-1 compare with other full-duplex models? Unlike traditional cascade voice agents that rely on intermediate speech-to-text and text-to-speech conversion steps, Tofu-1 processes audio directly. This architecture allows the model to maintain access to paralinguistic cues such as tone, hesitation, and background noise, while enabling the model to listen, reason, and speak simultaneously. The model is designed specifically for challenging telephony environments, including moving vehicles, hospital settings, and connections with weak signal integrity.

Technically, Tofu-1 features three primary audio processing capabilities: speaker tracking for identifying interlocutors and their targets, noise separation to isolate voices from environmental interference like highway traffic or intercoms, and paralinguistic analysis to detect user frustration or urgency. The model supports full-duplex interaction, allowing callers to interrupt or correct the agent mid-sentence without breaking the conversation flow. Additionally, the model can generate synthetic call environments, including background room noise and line interference. While Bland has not disclosed the internal architecture or parameter count, they have positioned Tofu-1 as the first in a planned family of speech-to-speech models, with deployment specifications available via the GPULeaderboard.com Chrome extension.
takeaways: **Architecture:** Tofu-1 utilizes a direct speech-to-speech pipeline, bypassing the latency and data loss associated with traditional text-based cascade models.
**Audio Capabilities:** The model includes specific features for speaker tracking, noise separation (e.g., crying children, TV audio, keypad tones), and paralinguistic detection.
**Competitive Landscape:** Tofu-1 is positioned against OpenAI's GPT-Live-1, NVIDIA's NemotronLabs VoiceChat 11B, and Block Dessa's model, with Tofu-1 currently maintaining closed weights.
**TV Test:** Bland utilizes a 'TV Test' benchmark to evaluate the model's ability to maintain focus on a caller while ignoring louder, competing speech from a television background.

title: Where was Nvidia’s security team?
author: Connie Loizos
contentSnippet:
Outsiders had little reason to notice when Nvidia’s longtime chief security officer and head of product security stepped down in August. Just two and a half months later, CEO Jensen Huang himself left the company over growing questions about his extramarital relationships — starting with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore data center company that U.S. investigators suspect of funneling Nvidia chips to China, then widening to reports about two separate affairs with Nvidia employees.

At the time, David Reber, who spent four years as CSO and seven at Nvidia overall, said he was leaving for health reasons. “This wasn’t a pivot I had planned. But I know what needs to come first: family and health,” he wrote on LinkedIn in late August, disclosing that he’d been diagnosed with young-onset Parkinson’s more than two years ago.

Reber’s replacement, Saša Zdjelar, previously spent 17 years at ExxonMobil in Houston, leaving as a senior IT manager before spending one year at Salesforce and several years at the cybersecurity company ReversingLabs. Zdjelar didn’t respond to questions Thursday about the transition or what the security team knew.

Nothing public connects Reber’s or Zdjelar’s role changes to the Megaspeed matter, but it seems fair to wonder what Nvidia’s security team knew about the government’s scrutiny of Megaspeed and about Huang’s relationships, and whether anyone raised concerns. Reber didn’t respond to questions Thursday. Nvidia also has not answered our related questions.

Relationships between a CEO and his employees typically fall to HR, legal and the board, not security. But security specialists say any affair — even one inside the office — can give a foreign intelligence service leverage over an exec who wants it kept quiet. And Huang’s relationship with an executive at Megaspeed, a company under federal investigation, wasn’t an office matter at all. (Megaspeed has denied any wrongdoing.)

Still, spotting the clues isn’t easy. The way intelligence services collect information, much of it through everyday conversation rather than hacking, makes it especially difficult for security teams to identify risks, according to retired senior intelligence officer Nicholas Eftimiades, who says he has trained more than 1,000 corporate security professionals.

Some people inside Nvidia clearly knew parts of the picture. Nvidia’s top lawyer was engaged with

summary.tldr:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang resigned in October following reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including a relationship with an executive at Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center firm currently under U.S. federal investigation for allegedly funneling Nvidia chips to China. These revelations followed the August departure of Nvidia’s longtime Chief Security Officer, David Reber, who cited a diagnosis of young-onset Parkinson’s disease. While Nvidia’s legal team was reportedly aware of the Megaspeed inquiry over a year ago, it remains unclear if the company’s security apparatus was informed of the CEO’s personal relationships or the potential counterintelligence risks they posed.

Industry experts, including former intelligence officer Nicholas Eftimiades, note that corporate security teams often struggle to identify risks stemming from human intelligence operations, which frequently rely on long-term relationship cultivation rather than traditional cyber-hacking. The situation highlights a broader debate regarding the scope of corporate security, which is often limited to physical and cyber-defense rather than monitoring insider threats or executive vulnerabilities. As the Nvidia board conducts an independent investigation alongside federal inquiries, the case serves as a high-profile example of the challenges U.S. firms face regarding foreign intelligence efforts to gain policy and export control insights.
takeaways: **Leadership Transition:** David Reber served as Nvidia’s CSO for four years before stepping down in August; he was replaced by Saša Zdjelar, a former IT manager at ExxonMobil and executive at ReversingLabs.

**Alleged Conflicts:** Reports indicate Jensen Huang engaged in multiple affairs, including one with a direct-report vice president and another with an executive at Megaspeed, a company under federal scrutiny for potential export control violations.

**Intelligence Tactics:** Experts like Nicholas Eftimiades emphasize that foreign intelligence services, particularly those linked to China, increasingly utilize long-term human relationship cultivation and technical tools like IMSI catchers to gain policy insights and influence.

**Security Scope:** Corporate security specialists argue that many firms underfund security and define it too narrowly, focusing on facility and cyber protection while neglecting the monitoring of executive vulnerabilities and insider threats.

title: SALA: Semantically Aligned Latent Actions Enable Dual-Axis Scaling of Embodied Foundation Models
author: Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Haonan Wang, Zhijie Deng
contentSnippet:
Authors: Jiachun Jin , Zetong Zhou , Haonan Wang , Zhijie Deng

Abstract: Embodied foundation models hinge on diverse robot interaction data, which are costly to collect. Egocentric human videos offer a complementary source of experience, and latent action models (LAMs) provide a popular means of leveraging these videos for policy supervision. Compared with world-action models (WAMs), LAMs can offer greater training efficiency and potentially lower inference costs by avoiding explicit pixel prediction during policy learning and execution. However, most existing LAMs learn latent actions solely through video reconstruction, which can cause their representations to cluster by visual appearance rather than by the underlying actions. As a result, they struggle to align human actions with their robot counterparts. To bridge the gap, we introduce SALA, which emphasizes establishing the semantic correspondence for latent actions. Without requiring paired data, we use the language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to estimate semantic similarities and supervise cross-embodiment correspondence. Specifically, we translate these similarities into soft neighborhood structures that guide human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while robot action reconstruction grounds the latent space in control. The resulting shared latent action space provides a unified supervision signal for training an embodied foundation model on both human and robot videos. Notably, latent action supervision enables scaling along two axes: (1) pre-training on increasing amounts of general human video consistently reduces robot action prediction error on downstream tasks, and (2) post-training on increasing amounts of task-specific human video substantially improves real-world robot task success rates.

summary.tldr:
Researchers Jiachun Jin, Zetong Zhou, Haonan Wang, and Zhijie Deng have introduced SALA (Semantically Aligned Latent Actions), a framework designed to improve embodied foundation models by aligning human egocentric video data with robot control actions. Unlike traditional Latent Action Models (LAMs) that rely solely on visual reconstruction—often leading to representations clustered by appearance rather than action—SALA uses language descriptions of unpaired human and robot clips to establish semantic correspondence. By translating these semantic similarities into soft neighborhood structures, the model guides human latent actions toward semantically related robot latents, while simultaneously grounding the space in robot control through action reconstruction.

This approach enables dual-axis scaling for embodied foundation models. First, pre-training on large-scale general human video datasets consistently reduces robot action prediction error. Second, post-training on task-specific human video significantly boosts real-world robot task success rates. By avoiding explicit pixel prediction, SALA maintains the training efficiency and lower inference costs characteristic of LAMs while overcoming the cross-embodiment alignment gap that has historically limited the utility of human video in robotics.
takeaways: **Core Methodology:** SALA uses language-based semantic similarity to align human and robot latent actions without requiring paired training data.
**Dual-Axis Scaling:** The framework supports scaling via general human video pre-training to reduce prediction error and task-specific human video post-training to improve success rates.
**Architectural Advantage:** By focusing on latent action alignment rather than pixel-level world-action modeling (WAM), SALA achieves higher training efficiency and lower inference overhead.
**Supervision Mechanism:** The model employs soft neighborhood structures to bridge the semantic gap between human egocentric videos and robot control trajectories.

title: Centered Ablation: Why Last-Layer Directional Ablation Under-Fires or Collapses, and a Closed-Form Fix
author: Quy-Anh Dang, Chris Ngo
contentSnippet: Directional ablation removes a hidden state's component along a "behaviour direction" while a language model runs. It is the standard way to switch a behaviour such as refusal off, but it is erratic: on some models it barely fires, on others the text collapses into repetition. We show why, and fix it. At the last residual stream, ablation is exactly a logit bias: a fixed vocabulary footprint scaled by a gate, the cosine between the hidden state and the direction. The gate is measured from the origin, but last-layer states share a large common mode far from it, so a direction that overlaps the common mode fires on benign text and under-fires on its targets. Centered Ablation (CA) projects the common mode out of the direction, in closed form. Across 8 models, CA raises attack success by 29 and 46 points where the standard recipe under-fires, cuts collapse on Gemma-2-9B from 50\% to 1\%, and preserves 12 to 40 points more benign answers on high-overlap models, 39 to 46 more than the affine offset of prior work. Two numbers computed before generation predict, on models the analysis had not seen, which gain faithfulness and which gain attack success, and a collapse index marks when text degenerates. We also show that two standard safety judges score collapsed text in opposite directions, which can fabricate a 46-point effect.

title: SWE-CoWork: Benchmarking Coding Agents as Digital Employees in Organizations
author: Xinping Lei, Minghao Liu, Ruijie Zhu, Xiaohui Hu
contentSnippet: A coding agent working within a software organization must establish what to build, collaborate with colleagues, and verify what it delivers. We introduce SWE-CoWork, a benchmark comprising 101 development assignments across 101 real repositories, 11 programming languages, and 12 application domains. Each assignment places an agent in a simulated engineering organization with 26 colleagues who have distinct responsibilities, bounded knowledge, and controlled collaboration behavior. Starting from a brief handoff, agents must recover requirements distributed across colleagues and workplace records, reconcile conflicting evidence, and implement changes evaluated by private executable tests. We evaluate eleven models and find a substantial gap between partial implementation and complete task delivery. The two leading models satisfy approximately 63% of fail-to-pass (F2P) tests but complete fewer than 8% of assignments. Providing complete requirements upfront improves F2P by approximately 16 percentage points for Seed Evolving and GPT-6 Astra, yet leaves complete task success unchanged. Requirement-level trajectory analysis reveals failures throughout the delivery process: Claude-Opus-5.5 directs a mean of 93% of first questions about queried cards to their accountable owners across runs but obtains only 64% of colleague-held requirements. Deferred questions go unfollowed, implementations remain incomplete even after requirements are acquired, and 31% of requirements reported as completed fail their tests. These findings highlight sustained requirement tracking, from clarification through implementation, verification, and handoff, as a key challenge for reliable autonomous software engineering.

title: Reflection Anchors for Propagation-Aware Visual Retention in Long-Chain Multimodal Reasoning
author: Xuan Gong, Hanbo Huang, Hao Zheng, Yiran Zhang
contentSnippet: Long chain-of-thought (CoT) reasoning improves large vision--language models, but visual information often fades during generation, limiting long-horizon multimodal reasoning. Existing methods either re-inject vision at inference or train policies for stronger grounding, but where to intervene relies on perception heuristics rather than principled gain analysis, and how local visual influence propagates remains implicit. We study this problem from an information-theoretic standpoint and derive a lower bound on the downstream visual gain of a one-step intervention, which suggests two factors: local branching room (token entropy) and downstream visual propagation potential (suffix divergence from a vision-marginalized reference). Guided by this analysis, we propose reflection-anchor policy optimization (RAPO), a GRPO-based policy optimization method that selects high-entropy reflection anchors and optimizes a chain-masked finite-window KL surrogate for downstream visual dependence. Experiments on reasoning-intensive and general-domain benchmarks show that RAPO delivers substantial gains over strong baselines across multiple LVLM backbones. Mechanism analyses further indicate that reflection anchors are enriched for visually sensitive decision points and that RAPO increases contrastive visual-dependence signals along generated trajectories.

title: GlyphAtlas: Disentangling Stroke Detail from Layout for Scene Text Synthesis
author: Luozheng Qin, Changhai Zhou, Yiyi Zhou
contentSnippet: Scene text synthesis requires stroke-accurate characters rendered in a specified layout, as well as visual coherence with the surrounding scene. To achieve this, existing methods commonly pre-render the target text at its intended locations to form a glyph image that jointly specifies layout and glyph structure. However, this representation ties the resolution of each glyph to its target region, limiting fine-grained stroke guidance for small, densely packed, or structurally complex text. To tackle this, we propose GlyphAtlas, a scene text synthesis framework that retains the glyph image as a spatial anchor and supplies fine-grained stroke references through a dedicated glyph atlas. The atlas renders and encodes each character or word in a separate cell, decoupling reference resolution from target-region size. We further introduce atlas-anchored attention, which lets each text region retrieve stroke detail only from its corresponding atlas cells to refine the coarse glyph structure provided by the glyph image. This coarse-to-fine conditioning simplifies stroke rendering while preserving explicit layout correspondence. We optimize GlyphAtlas with a mask-weighted flow matching objective and a timestep-weighted text perceptual loss for writing accuracy and background consistency. Random resolution augmentation of atlas cells supports adjustable atlas budgets at inference. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GlyphAtlas achieves stroke-accurate synthesis of small, dense, and structurally complex text, zero-shot transfer to languages unseen during task-specific training, and leading performance in scenes with many text regions. project page: https://fr0zencrane.github.io/project-glyphatlas/

title: AllocFlow: End-to-End Portfolio Trading Action Generation from Raw Market Data
author: Annan Wang, Yuchen Xie, Yu Cen, Leon Liangyu Chen
contentSnippet: Real-world portfolio management requires converting noisy market observations into coordinated, simultaneous allocations across multiple assets under shared capital constraints. Advances in forecasting models and alpha discovery help identify opportunities. However, traditional pipelines often decouple signal forecasting from portfolio construction, potentially misaligning learning with allocation and execution objectives. We present AllocFlow, an end-to-end flow-matching framework that directly generates joint portfolio allocations from raw multi-asset market histories. To capture dependencies among portfolio positions, AllocFlow employs a cross-asset flow Transformer conditioned on temporal market representations to generate continuous, signed position weights across all instruments jointly. To address the sample inefficiency and instability of learning continuous allocation policies from scratch, we establish a two-stage training scheme: strategy-supervised imitation shapes a structured distribution of candidate portfolios, followed by group-relative reinforcement learning (RL) that refines joint decisions using portfolio-level financial rewards and a frozen policy reference. On hourly cryptocurrency perpetual futures, RL refinement raises the annualized net return of the imitation policy from 27.79% to 51.38% and its Calmar ratio from 0.955 to 4.043, surpassing the teacher strategy on every metric, and AllocFlow reaches a Calmar ratio of 4.90 on six further months of unseen 2026 data without retraining.

title: VoxMel TTS Technical Report
author: Wenhao Guan, Jiaxin Ye, Haitao Li, Yifan Duan
contentSnippet: Continuous autoregressive TTS relies on an acoustic target that enables stable next-latent modeling while preserving fine-grained acoustic details. While existing approaches employ learned compressed representations (e.g., continuous VAE latents) to render prediction tractable, they rely on complex neural encoders that often cap generation fidelity. Conversely, training-free targets like mel-spectrograms eliminate encoder overhead, yet their potential for autoregressive generation remains largely underexplored. In this work, we propose VoxMel, a tokenizer-free framework for autoregressive TTS that makes stable mel modeling tractable through a fixed, exactly invertible two-axis Haar transform. The transform first decomposes each mel spectrogram along frequency into local averages and a frequency residual, then splits the averaged component along time into Coarse-Mel and a temporal residual. A language-model backbone with a flow-matching head autoregressively generates Coarse-Mel. Non-autoregressive residual tiers then predict the temporal residual from Coarse-Mel, followed by the frequency residual conditioned on the reconstructed Frequency-Averaged Mel. Neither residual is fed back into the autoregressive history. Trained on 100K hours of Emilia, the supervised 0.6B model obtains 1.51\% WER and 0.738 speaker similarity (SIM) on test-en, and 1.29\% CER and 0.755 SIM on test-zh. GRPO improves these results to 1.15\% WER / 0.753 SIM and 1.17\% CER / 0.776 SIM, respectively. We also distill the guided flow head into two- and four-step students, requiring 2 or 4 head evaluations per coarse frame. The four-step student retains competitive SIM and nearly matches the supervised model in WER/CER.

title: Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang
author: Anthony Ha
contentSnippet: Posted: 1:41 PM PST · November 14, 2026 Image Credits: Li Hongbo/VCG / Getty Images Anthony Ha Elon Musk, other tech execs sign petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate Jensen Huang A petition calling on Nvidia to reinstate the company’s recently ousted CEO Jensen Huang appears to have attracted more than 115,000 signatures as of Saturday afternoon. The petition website said the signers include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. Notable supporters include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. The petition states that its signers are “concerned that Jensen was removed without meaningful due process” and demands that the board “bring him back while an independent investigation establishes the facts.” It also calls on the board to ensure a fair investigation and provide more information to the public. “Jensen deserves due process, not mob justice,” the petition says. Huang resigned on Thursday , four days after confessing to having an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence to be a Chinese spy. The former CEO has agreed to testify before Congress, while news reports have also suggested that Huang engaged in multiple extramarital affairs . Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as the company’s interim CEO while it searches for a permanent replacement. Nvidia’s stock price fell sharply through the week, while Huang’s departure is also expected to leave a big gap in AI industry funding . Newsletters See More Subscribe for the industry’s biggest tech news Related Venture Jensen Huang’s departure blasts big hole in AI startup funding, VCs and founders say AI The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline Amanda Silberling

summary.tldr:
A petition demanding the reinstatement of former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has garnered over 115,000 signatures as of November 14, 2026. The signatories include 5,965 current Nvidia employees, 1,108 former employees, and 63,063 shareholders. High-profile supporters of the movement include Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk, Replit CEO Amjad Masad, Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney, and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan. The petition organizers argue that Huang was removed without sufficient due process and are calling for his return pending an independent investigation into the circumstances surrounding his departure.

Huang resigned on November 12, 2026, following his admission of an extramarital affair with a chip industry executive who is reportedly under investigation by U.S. intelligence for suspected ties to Chinese espionage. Subsequent reports have alleged that Huang was involved in multiple extramarital affairs. In the wake of his resignation, Nvidia’s board appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO while initiating a search for a permanent successor. The leadership transition has triggered a sharp decline in Nvidia’s stock price and raised significant concerns regarding the future of AI industry funding, which had been heavily influenced by Huang's tenure.
takeaways: **Petition Metrics:** The campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang reached 115,000 signatures, including support from 5,965 current and 1,108 former Nvidia staff.
**Leadership Transition:** Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has been named interim CEO following Huang's resignation on November 12, 2026.
**Core Allegations:** Huang's resignation followed his admission of an affair with a chip executive suspected by U.S. intelligence of being a Chinese spy.
**Industry Impact:** The departure has resulted in a sharp decline in Nvidia's stock price and is projected to create a significant funding gap for AI startups.
**Congressional Oversight:** The former CEO has agreed to provide testimony before the U.S. Congress regarding the scandal.

title: AT&T uses agentic AI to reinvent business processes from the ground up
author: Paul Gillin
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 14:37 EST / NOVEMBER 14 2026

AT&T uses agentic AI to reinvent business processes from the ground up

AT&T Corp. is moving beyond using artificial intelligence to improve employee productivity, increasingly applying autonomous agents to redesign how its business operates. Nearly 500 agentic workflows are already in production, and the telecom giant plans to triple that number next year.

AT&T now processes about 45 billion AI tokens daily across the company, according to Luke Corbin (pictured, below), assistant vice president of digital transformation and AI at AT&T Business. Its agentic AI platform handles more than 1 million transactions monthly. Many of those workflows now operate autonomously, handling tasks ranging from customer provisioning to sales prospecting.

Speaking at an Amazon Web Services Inc. event in Boston earlier this month, Corbin said the company’s approach emphasizes rethinking entire processes rather than simply automating individual tasks. AT&T has moved quickly from experimenting with generative AI to systematically identifying business processes that can be redesigned around agentic capabilities.

At the heart of the transformation is Business Agent Foundry, a group established in early 2025 to work with individual business units. Rather than soliciting isolated automation ideas from employees, the foundry maps business processes using industry frameworks and identifies opportunities to eliminate unnecessary steps, organizational handoffs and legacy application dependencies, Corbin said.

One early initiative involved automating interactions with AT&T’s mainframe computers. Changes to customer fiber installation orders previously required employees to retrieve tickets from queues, manually update records and return them to the workflow.

Agentic automation eliminated portions of that manual process, reducing delays and accelerating service delivery.

“It was kind of cool having some of the most advanced technology talking to some of the oldest that we have,” Corbin said.

In another example, AT&T halved the time required to provision dedicated internet connections in buildings where fiber infrastructure was already installed.

summary.tldr:
AT&T is shifting its AI strategy from simple productivity tools to autonomous agentic workflows, with nearly 500 workflows currently in production and plans to triple that count in 2026. According to Luke Corbin, assistant vice president of digital transformation and AI at AT&T Business, the company processes approximately 45 billion AI tokens daily and handles over 1 million transactions monthly via its agentic platform. The initiative is managed by the 'Business Agent Foundry,' established in early 2025, which focuses on redesigning end-to-end business processes rather than automating isolated tasks, specifically targeting the elimination of legacy application dependencies and organizational handoffs.

Technically, AT&T avoids the common approach of deploying massive fleets of specialized agents. Instead, it utilizes a smaller set of agents that execute workflows based on centrally managed business logic stored in context or memory. The architecture separates concerns into retrieval agents, which identify knowledge, and planning agents, which determine necessary tools and data. Governance is strictly tiered: while employees can build personal productivity agents, customer-facing or business-critical workflows must pass through the foundry for security, privacy, and compliance reviews. Production workflows require human oversight until they achieve mid-to-high 90% accuracy, at which point they transition to autonomous operation with continuous monitoring for performance drift.
takeaways: **Operational Scale:** AT&T currently processes 45 billion AI tokens daily and manages over 1 million monthly transactions through its agentic platform.
**Architectural Strategy:** The company utilizes a centralized business logic model rather than a large, fragmented fleet of independent agents.
**Performance Metrics:** Production AI investments are reportedly achieving a fivefold return on investment within a one-year timeframe.
**Deployment Threshold:** Autonomous operation is only permitted after a workflow demonstrates mid-to-high 90% accuracy under human supervision.
**Process Optimization:** Agentic workflows have successfully halved the time required to provision dedicated internet connections in buildings with existing fiber infrastructure.

title: The AI graveyard: a running list of projects and startups that didn’t make it
author: Lauren Forristal
contentSnippet:
Last month, chatbot platform Character.ai filed for bankruptcy just five years after launching. More recently, privacy-focused AI assistant Ollie announced its shutdown a few weeks ago.

Aside from Character.ai and Ollie, plenty of AI bets never even survive inside the companies that build them. According to S&P Global Market Intelligence , about 42% of AI initiatives are ultimately abandoned by their corporate parents. The reasons vary: insufficient funding, technical challenges, competition, difficulty scaling, or just weak user demand.

The result is a growing AI graveyard. Below is a look at some of the most notable AI products, startups, launches, and bets that have shut down, pivoted, or significantly missed expectations. Think of it less as a scorecard of flops than as a record of what these attempts can (hopefully) teach the rest of the industry.

OpenAI has taken several stumbles

Even the biggest players aren’t immune. OpenAI, one of the most valuable private companies in the world, has had its own share of casualties and missteps. One of the more recent examples was its attempt to turn ChatGPT into a broader “ super app .” On July 9, OpenAI updated the app to combine several experiences, including separate “Chat,” “Codex,” and “Work” modes, while renaming the traditional, familiar version “ChatGPT Classic.”

The redesign quickly drew criticism from users who found the new interface confusing and cluttered, and OpenAI rolled back the change soon after , bringing the familiar ChatGPT interface back.

That wasn’t OpenAI’s only attempt to pull everything under one roof. The company has also shut down several stand-alone apps and folded their features directly into ChatGPT — a strategy that’s worked out better than the redesign did. ChatGPT Atlas, a stand-alone AI-powered web browser, lasted less than a year before being discontinued on August 9, with its most useful features absorbed into ChatGPT.

The company did the same thing with Operator , an AI agent that could browse the web and complete tasks on a user’s behalf, and OpenAI has increasingly built image generation directly into ChatGPT, shrinking the role of DALL-E as its own separate destination for creating images.

We also can’t forget its video-sharing platform, Sora , which struggled with high operating costs and user-retention challenges and shut down in March 2026.
