This headroom slows prefill, so \sysname serves the shortest waiting prompt first.
When TTFT deadlines grow with prompt length, the long prompts it delays have the most time to spare.
Under disaggregation, it spaces admissions so that no request waits on more slow admission steps than its P99 target allows.

title: Windows 0-day dropped by disgruntled researcher hands hackers System rights
author: Dan Goodin
contentSnippet:
Nightmare Eclipse, the pseudonym of a researcher with an ongoing, very public beef with Microsoft, has dropped yet another Windows zero-day.

On Tuesday, Nightmare Eclipse disclosed SignDrop, a vulnerability that gives local users full System rights on some versions of Windows. The vulnerability resides in the Common Log File System , which Microsoft describes as a “general-purpose logging service used by software clients running in user-mode or kernel-mode.” By forcing a privileged process such as Windows Defender to open a crafted CLFS container, an attacker with ordinary user rights can abuse the privileged file creation to elevate privileges to System.

Turning a Windows defense against itself

The attack exploits the interaction of CLFS, Windows Defender, and Windows file permissions. The exploit uses Windows Defender to open a log file created by a standard user by calling ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature, a legitimate Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates.

By manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links, the attacker causes Defender to open the CLFS container in the security context of the antimalware engine. If an associated authentication file is missing, CLFS creates it using Defender’s System privileges. Because CLFS assigns the newly created file the Discretionary Access Control List of the original file, the attacker may gain access to a file created with System privileges, allowing the file-creation operation to be abused as part of a privilege-escalation attack.

Ironically, the vulnerability stems from a security measure Microsoft introduced in October 2025 to prevent attackers from exploiting other vulnerabilities in CLFS.

“If everything is chained correctly, funnily this legit security mitigation can be used against itself and allow an elevation [of] privileges,” Nightmare Eclipse wrote . “Everything is done properly by Microsoft here but the logic allows abuse.”

What makes it funnier is the fact that it can be used against any antimalware engine to bypass their self defense (or tamper protection) mechanism as you can trigger arbitrary file creation in the context of their own antimalware process so from the perspective of their kernel drivers, the file creation request is coming from their own legit process so it passes, this makes this vulnerability unique as it can be used to turn off any antivirus/EDR.

Nigh

summary.tldr:
An independent researcher operating under the pseudonym Nightmare Eclipse disclosed a Windows zero-day vulnerability named SignDrop, which grants local users full System privileges. The flaw resides within the Common Log File System (CLFS) and weaponizes a security mitigation introduced by Microsoft in October 2025. By manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links and invoking ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature—a legitimate Windows Defender function for processing antivirus signature updates—an attacker forces a privileged process to open a crafted CLFS container, enabling arbitrary file creation under System context.

The vulnerability allows local attackers to bypass self-defense and tamper-protection mechanisms of antivirus and Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) solutions, as file creation requests originate from the legitimate antimalware process itself. According to the disclosure and analysis by researcher Will Dormann, the exploit affects Windows 11 26H2, Windows 11 26H2 Experimental, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental. However, Dormann noted specific prerequisites for successful exploitation, including that the target Windows 26H2 system must have existed for more than 90 days and the registry key HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode must be set to 0 or 1.

Microsoft stated it is currently investigating the disclosure, confirmed it has no evidence of active exploitation in the wild, and maintained that Windows Defender blocks potential exploitation attempts. Users can verify vulnerability status by checking the CLFS authentication mode, where learning or enforcement modes indicate vulnerability alongside the provided proof-of-concept script.
takeaways: **Vulnerability Name and Impact:** SignDrop is a local privilege escalation zero-day discovered by researcher Nightmare Eclipse that grants standard local users full System rights and allows the disabling of arbitrary antivirus and EDR solutions.
**Affected Operating Systems:** The exploit targets Windows 11 26H2, Windows 11 26H2 Experimental, and Windows Server 2025 Experimental.

**Exploit Mechanism:** The attack forces Windows Defender to open a crafted Common Log File System (CLFS) container by abusing ServerMpUpdateEngineSignature and manipulating Windows Object Manager symbolic links.

**Exploitation Requirements:** Researcher Will Dormann verified the exploit requires a Windows 26H2 system that has existed for more than 90 days, with the registry value HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SYSTEM\CurrentControlSet\Services\CLFS\Authentication\Mode set to 0 or 1.

title: Perplexity Releases Decider v1.3: Open-Weight Decision Models Add Locate
author: Asif Razzaq
contentSnippet: Perplexity has released pplx-decider-v1.3 and pplx-decider-flash-v1.3 , the latest versions of its open-weight decision models. Perplexity Decider v1.3 is a decision model that returns probabilities, not generated text. It answers yes/no, multiple-choice and score questions about a text or image input. The main addition is Locate, which extracts exact text spans by type or instruction. Weights ship under Apache 2.0 on Hugging Face . Both models also run in the Perplexity Decisions API and on OpenRouter . You can check the deployment options and specs here through our GPULeaderboard.com chrome extension . TL;DR Size: 27B on Qwen3.8-27B ; Flash is 4B on Qwen3.5-4B . Hugging Face lists 26B and 5B params. API input: under 256K tokens. Local default: 32,768. Runs on: a CUDA GPU fitting ~49 GiB of BF16 weights (v1.3) or ~8.5 GiB (Flash). No quantized variants. Performance: leads TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14 on most of Perplexity’s self-reported evaluations. Best: 91.6% mean accuracy on 63 query-classification tasks. Worst: Locate averages 69.0, its lowest absolute score. Flash trails Jev 1.14 in finance, programming and law. Bottom line: Best: a 0.27% answer-flip rate and $26.47 per 1M production requests. Worst: every figure is self-reported. What is Perplexity Decider v1.3? Decider is Perplexity’s family of decision models, inspired by TypeSafe’s Jev . Each request has a shared ‘state’ plus one or more questions with labeled options. The model returns a probability per option instead of writing an answer. v1.3 succeeds v1.2 and Flash v1.2 . Flash v1.3 is distilled from the large model. How does Decider v1.3 work? Perplexity adapts a generative LLM backbone into a classifier. The output layer starts from the base model’s LM head, pruned to option tokens (A, B, C). A linear decision head reads the hidden state at a <|marker|> token and outputs option probabilities. Full-attention layers are made bidirectional, which Perplexity’s ablations showed helps. v1.3 also changes attention between questions. In v1.2, every question saw every other question, so answers could shift. In v1.3, the state sees all questions, but each question sees only the state and itself. All questions about one input still run in a single forward pass. Training runs in 3 stages: a full fine-tune on hundreds of public datasets a LoRA specialization adapter a LoRA vision adapter Weights are averaged acro

summary.tldr:
Perplexity has released pplx-decider-v1.3 and its distilled counterpart, pplx-decider-flash-v1.3, as open-weight decision models under the Apache 2.0 license. Unlike standard generative LLMs, these models function as classifiers that return probabilities for yes/no, multiple-choice, and scoring tasks rather than generating text. The v1.3 release introduces a 'Locate' feature for extracting specific text spans based on instructions. The models are built on Qwen backbones, with the 27B version (v1.3) utilizing Qwen3.8-27B and the 4B version (Flash) utilizing Qwen3.5-4B. Weights are available on Hugging Face, and the models are accessible via the Perplexity Decisions API and OpenRouter.

Technically, the architecture adapts a generative LLM backbone by pruning the LM head to specific option tokens and adding a linear decision head that reads hidden states. Perplexity modified the attention mechanism from v1.2; while v1.2 allowed all questions to attend to one another, v1.3 restricts each question to attend only to the shared state and itself, preventing cross-question answer shifting while maintaining single-pass inference. The models support up to 256K tokens for API inputs and 32,768 tokens for local defaults. Training involves a three-stage process: a full fine-tune on public datasets, followed by LoRA specialization and vision adapters. The models require approximately 49 GiB of VRAM for the 27B version and 8.5 GiB for the Flash version in BF16 precision.
takeaways: **Model Architecture:** The 27B model is based on Qwen3.8-27B, while the 4B Flash model is distilled from the larger version using Qwen3.5-4B.
**Performance Metrics:** The v1.3 model achieves a 91.6% mean accuracy on 63 query-classification tasks, with a 0.27% answer-flip rate, outperforming TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14 in most internal benchmarks.
**Inference Requirements:** The 27B model requires ~49 GiB of BF16 VRAM, while the 4B Flash model requires ~8.5 GiB; no quantized variants are currently provided.
**Attention Mechanism:** v1.3 implements bidirectional full-attention layers and restricts inter-question attention to prevent answer interference, unlike the v1.2 architecture.
**Pricing:** The API is priced at $26.47 per 1 million production requests.

title: ChatGPT’s new Wallet lets AI agents shop and check out for you
author: Sarah Perez
contentSnippet:
ChatGPT can now shop for you. On Friday, OpenAI launched a new wallet feature that lets its agents, called dots , help you decide what to buy and then complete the purchase on your behalf. The option will initially be available to a limited number of U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers, ages 18 and up, with a U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express.

OpenAI says that users are fully in control of the purchases, as they’re able to review the items, the total, and the payment card that will be used to complete the transaction before the checkout occurs. In addition, users will approve the purchases directly with a security check like Face ID or a fingerprint, which creates a record of their transaction.

The addition comes as consumer-facing AI tools are working to find the right product-market fit, in terms of how they can help people be more efficient as they complete various tasks. While companies like DoorDash and Uber have so far reported low numbers of orders placed by AI agents, Meta’s Muse, which now has over 10 million users, has seen AI-assisted shopping become a top activity on its app.

Other personal AI agents, like Instinct, also support making purchases on users’ behalf.

It’s no surprise, then, that OpenAI would want to enter this space more with an agentic shopping feature of its own.

To get started, ChatGPT subscribers add their eligible payment cards to the new ChatGPT Wallet, then ask their dot to help with a purchase. (This setup is a one-time thing; users don’t have to re-enter their payment information every time they buy.) When it’s time to transact, ChatGPT’s Wallet charges the selected card using a payment token, which is a substitute for the user’s actual card details, so that information isn’t shared with either the dot or the merchant.

The merchant will automatically receive what it needs to fulfill the order from the dot, like the shipping address and contact information, OpenAI says. The company notes that customers who shop via their dots will still be able to earn their credit card rewards and be able to take advantage of protections that typically come with cards, like being able to dispute transactions.

The limited availability at launch will allow OpenAI to test and improve the feature and its capabilities before rolling it out more broadly. In the future, the company plans to offer users more control over the feature

summary.tldr:
OpenAI has introduced a new 'Wallet' feature for ChatGPT, enabling AI agents—referred to as 'dots'—to facilitate and complete consumer purchases. The feature is currently in limited release for U.S.-based ChatGPT Pro subscribers aged 18 and older, supporting U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, and American Express cards. Users must manually authorize each transaction via biometric security checks, such as Face ID or fingerprint scanning, after reviewing the item, total cost, and payment method.

Technically, the system utilizes payment tokens to process transactions, ensuring that sensitive card details are not shared with the AI agent or the merchant. The 'dot' agent handles the transmission of necessary fulfillment data, such as shipping addresses and contact information, to the retailer. OpenAI maintains that users retain standard credit card rewards and consumer protections, including the ability to dispute transactions. To support broader adoption, OpenAI has released a 'Commerce Partner Playbook' to assist retailers in integrating with agentic commerce, though the company faces competition and resistance from major retailers like Amazon, which currently blocks AI agents to prioritize its own Alexa ecosystem.
takeaways: **Security Architecture:** Transactions are processed via payment tokens to mask actual card details from merchants and the AI agent.
**User Authorization:** Every purchase requires a manual biometric confirmation (Face ID or fingerprint) by the user before the transaction is finalized.
**Eligibility:** The feature is restricted to U.S. ChatGPT Pro subscribers using U.S.-issued Visa, Mastercard, or American Express cards.
**Future Roadmap:** OpenAI plans to introduce configurable spending limits and automated purchase parameters to allow for higher levels of agent autonomy.
**Retailer Integration:** OpenAI published a 'Commerce Partner Playbook' to provide guidance for retailers looking to support agent-based shopping.

title: The unfolding Jensen Huang scandal: a timeline
author: Amanda Silberling
contentSnippet:
Nvidia co-founder and now former CEO Jensen Huang has never been as prone to controversy as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. But the 63-year-old industry kingpin recently admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in affairs that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and U.S. national security.

U.S. officials believe that one of Huang’s likely romantic interests, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed is a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company that reportedly purchased $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China. The Justice Department has since taken over the federal investigation into the company, The New York Times has reported.

The story took a sudden turn on Wednesday. Citing five people who worked at Nvidia, the Times reported that Huang also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company’s vice president of healthcare, who reports directly to him. Nvidia, Huang and Powell have not confirmed the report. Reached by a Times reporter, Huang reportedly said, “I don’t think you should be talking to me directly,” before hanging up.

By early Thursday morning, Huang was no longer CEO of the company he co-founded 33 years ago. Then, Thursday afternoon, Reuters dropped another bombshell, publishing a report alleging that Huang had yet another extramarital affair with another unnamed Nvidia employee.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

November 13, 2026: Huang was not confident in his successor, Colette Kress; reports describe Huang

summary.tldr:
Jensen Huang has resigned as CEO of Nvidia following a series of revelations regarding extramarital affairs and potential national security risks. Reports indicate Huang engaged in relationships with Kimberly Powell, Nvidia’s VP of Healthcare, an unnamed Nvidia employee, and Alice Huang, an executive at Singapore-based Megaspeed. U.S. officials allege Alice Huang is a Chinese spy who facilitated the acquisition of $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips for entities in China, bypassing U.S. export controls. The Justice Department is currently investigating Megaspeed’s role in these chip transfers.

Following the resignation on November 12, 2026, Nvidia appointed CFO Colette Kress as interim CEO and named Harvey C. Jones as the company’s first-ever board chair. The fallout has triggered a broader political investigation, with Democrats and Republicans in Congress demanding testimony from Huang and Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick. Allegations have surfaced that the Trump administration permitted the sale of H200 AI chips to China in December 2025 in exchange for a portion of export sales, despite being briefed on Huang’s alleged compromising relationships. Huang is scheduled to testify before Congress regarding these matters before November 26, 2026.
takeaways: **Leadership Transition:** Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO, while Harvey C. Jones, a board member since 1993, has been appointed as the first-ever chair of the board.

**Export Control Allegations:** Reports suggest the Trump administration authorized the sale of H200 chips to China in December 2025, allegedly in exchange for a cut of export sales, despite intelligence regarding Huang's associations.
**Financial Impact:** Nvidia stock fell approximately 8% in after-hours trading on November 11, 2026, and saw an 11% decline over the five-day period surrounding the initial reports.

**Regulatory Scrutiny:** The Justice Department is investigating Megaspeed International, a firm linked to Alice Huang, which reportedly facilitated the acquisition of $7.5 billion in Nvidia chips, including restricted hardware, via entities like Shanghai Century Litong.

title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations
author: Robert Hof
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 10:00 EST / NOVEMBER 13 2026

Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s abrupt departure shakes AI industry’s foundations

THIS WEEK IN ENTERPRISE by Robert Hof

Honeypot or not, the Chinese executive/accused spy with whom Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted an affair this week should have been a flashing red light to him. So should fraternizing with one of your own VPs — and reportedly another employee too!

In the end, all that, and maybe more to come, was just too much for Nvidia’s board to bear despite the commanding position Huang (pictured) held not only at Nvidia but in the entire artificial intelligence industry. Indeed, the speed with which he resigned — spectacularly stupid as his behavior was — still makes me wonder if there are other shoes to drop, especially on the legal or national security fronts. Market researcher SemiAnalysis thinks it came down to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community that’s very unhappy Nvidia chips have apparently been smuggled to China.

Huang was something of an AI puppet master, providing the chips and software to power the entire industry as well as seemingly unlimited cash to fund and backstop everyone from AI leaders such as OpenAI and Anthropic to innumerable cloud compute providers worldwide. No single person inside or outside Nvidia seems likely to fill that role.

However, Nvidia really is much more than Jensen Huang. Interim CEO and CFO Colette Kress helped craft the financial arrangements that in part put Nvidia at the center of AI — though for what it’s worth, Huang himself wasn’t a fan lately . Some of his direct reports such as high-performance computing chief Ian Buck seem quite capable of carrying on, if perhaps not with Huang’s panache. One company is never one person, and shouldn’t be. I expect a less centralized Nvidia going forward, whoever’s at the top.

More than that, AI is much more than Jensen Huang, and it will continue to be going forward. It’s easy to forget that although Huang brilliantly helped create this new wave, AI and its enablers also are what made him a rock star. But that time is now over. Nvidia and certainly the AI industry shouldn’t be depending on one person to keep everything afloat anyway.

The reverberations of his sudden and shocking departure will continue to echo for a long time to come across Nvidia, its investors watching hundreds of billions of market cap evaporate, legions

summary.tldr:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned following a series of scandals involving extramarital affairs, including one with a suspected Chinese intelligence operative. The board of directors moved to oust Huang amid reports of multiple affairs and potential national security concerns regarding the illicit smuggling of Nvidia hardware into China. CFO Colette Kress has been appointed interim CEO, with high-performance computing chief Ian Buck noted as a key internal leader. Market analysts, including SemiAnalysis, suggest the departure may be linked to pressure from the U.S. intelligence community regarding export control compliance.

Despite the leadership vacuum, the broader AI sector continues to move forward. Anthropic has officially launched its IPO roadshow with a target valuation exceeding $64 billion, scheduled for next Thursday. Other market activity includes positive earnings guidance from CoreWeave and Cerebras, the latter of which announced a new deal with Microsoft. Conversely, companies with direct ties to Nvidia, such as Nebius and CoreWeave, experienced stock volatility following the news of Huang's resignation.
takeaways: **Leadership Transition:** CFO Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO following Jensen Huang's resignation.
**Anthropic IPO:** The company is seeking to raise over $64 billion in its upcoming initial public offering.
**Market Performance:** Cerebras shares rose nearly 18% following positive guidance and a Microsoft partnership, while Nebius shares dropped 17% after lowering its outlook.

**Recent Funding Rounds:** Notable capital raises include Mirendil ($1B), Mercor ($750M at $20B valuation), LangChain ($300M), Databento ($100M at $1.1B valuation), and Rox ($100M at $1.3B valuation).
**Industry Forecasts:** Gartner projects that AI infrastructure will account for 59% of total global AI spending by 2027.

title: ElevenLabs’ new app combines meeting note-taking and dictation for teams
author: Ivan Mehta

ElevenLabs also allows companies to integrate ElevenAgent and take follow-up actions such as writing a draft email based on meeting notes.

Plus, there’s a dictation feature, which lets users convert speech to cleaned-up text in any app with support for over 90 languages. The company said that the app is capable of understanding industry-specific terms across dictation and meeting transcription.

ElevenAI allows the company to use its own model as a showcase and also utilize its agent platforms for better context funneling. The startup’s positioning might not be to directly compete in the productivity market, but rather to give enterprise teams an option to not buy licenses to a notetaker and use its solution instead. All meeting-related tools are rushing to become central knowledge hubs for companies while aiming to automate knowledge extraction and follow-up actions

In the last week, the company also launched its v3 series of Scribe speech-to-text models with live transcription capabilities and the ability for companies to fine-tune models using their own data, a tool to pick the right language model based on use case , and a routine creator that automates tasks based on the transcript.

title: Agents idling while they wait on humans push Kubernetes to hand back unused resources
author: Jonathan Anthony
contentSnippet:
UPDATED 09:22 EST / NOVEMBER 13 2026

Agents idling while they wait on humans push Kubernetes to hand back unused resources

Agentic AI workloads are handing Kubernetes an unexpected second act . The orchestrator once dismissed as reliable but boring is now at the center of how enterprises plan to run autonomous software.

Past platform shifts, from physical servers to virtual machines and from virtual machines to containers, forced companies to wipe the slate clean and start over. This shift is different because Kubernetes was built as a platform for building platforms, according to Bobby Allen (pictured), cloud therapist at Google Cloud LLC.

“Kubernetes now, 11, 12+ years in, has this whole new life,” Allen said. “You don’t need a new platform this time. … This shift doesn’t mean that you’ve got to retool and rebuild and replatform everything, and I think that could be comforting for folks to realize that they don’t have to start from scratch.”

Allen spoke with theCUBE’s Rebecca Knight at KubeCon + CloudNativeCon NA , during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed how Kubernetes is recovering resources spent on idle agentic AI workloads. (* Disclosure below.)

Running agentic AI workloads in the open

Google is putting that view into practice. The company has donated Agent Substrate, gVisor and OpenRL to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation, while engineering teams are tuning Kubernetes for agents rather than building a new stack.

“Google is doubling down on our commitment to not just open source but community-driven, collaborative, multiple-partner-involvement open source,” Allen said. “These concepts are foundational, but they’re important enough that we need to all contribute and shape these together.”

Efficiency is a big part of the motivation. Agents spend long stretches idle while they wait for human input, and the projects aim to give those resources back during the downtime, Allen explained.

“These are kind of different efforts that contribute to an open, flexible, transparent, collaborative way to make agentic workloads run better so that we can have these amazing outcomes but also be efficient with our resources,” Allen said. “We don’t want to have this sci-fi Star Trek moment where we’re stepping into the future and kill the planet.”

Here’s the complete video interview, part of SiliconA

summary.tldr:
Google Cloud is positioning Kubernetes as the primary orchestration layer for agentic AI workloads, aiming to avoid the need for new, specialized infrastructure platforms. Bobby Allen, a cloud therapist at Google Cloud, stated that Kubernetes' maturity allows it to adapt to agent-based architectures without requiring enterprises to rebuild their existing stacks. The core technical challenge addressed is the inefficiency of AI agents that remain idle while awaiting human input, which currently consumes significant compute resources.

To optimize these workloads, Google has donated three key projects to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF): Agent Substrate, gVisor, and OpenRL. These projects are designed to improve the efficiency, transparency, and flexibility of agentic AI execution. By integrating these tools, Google aims to enable Kubernetes to dynamically reclaim resources during agent downtime, ensuring that large-scale AI deployments remain resource-efficient rather than relying on static, over-provisioned infrastructure.
takeaways: **Project Donations:** Google has contributed Agent Substrate, gVisor, and OpenRL to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation to support agentic AI on Kubernetes.
**Resource Optimization:** The initiative focuses on reclaiming compute resources from AI agents during idle periods while they wait for human interaction.
**Platform Strategy:** Google advocates for evolving Kubernetes rather than creating new platforms, citing the orchestrator's 11-12 year maturity as a stable foundation for autonomous software.
**Sustainability Goal:** The effort is framed as a move to prevent excessive resource consumption and environmental impact associated with scaling agentic AI workloads.

takeaways: **Version Policy:** Implementation of semantic versioning for llama.cpp and ggml, requiring major-version bumps for any API or ABI incompatibilities.

title: Claude’s Duet agent is a little neurotic and surprisingly helpful
author: Allison Johnson
contentSnippet: Normally, the products I test don’t offer to help me write up my experience with them. Duet is different. Claude Duet is Anthropic’s AI agent for consumers, the latest attempt by an AI company to try to convince us that agents can be useful for people who don’t write code. It’s been an interesting couple of months: Instinct gave us an impressive text-based assistant, Meta offered us its cute little guy, Muse, to help us buy things, and OpenAI gave us the more work-oriented Dots. Claude Duet is even more focused on work than those. It’s also more consumer-friendly than Claude Cowork, which was more consumer-friendly than Claude Code — the coding agent that kicked off a whole hype cycle earlier this year. I’ve been testing it over the past week as I navigate a busy travel and work schedule. At turns it has been truly useful, kind of a nag, and very eager to write about itself. Duet is still a “research preview” according to Anthropic, and access is limited to Pro, Max, and Ultra subscribers in the US, with a waitlist to join. It’s not here to order you burritos, either; it’s for “professionals and small business owners” and is meant to use its judgment about what needs your attention most. Like Meta’s Muse, Duet has its own app. (If you’re keeping score at home, yes, it has been updated to fully support the iPhone Duo). Duet uses Claude’s characteristically cheery, minimalist design. The app is consumer-friendly and approachable. Once you’ve connected all the productivity and chat services you want, it’ll look for ways to help out with and suggest them as cards you can swipe left or right to hide or accept — kind of a to-do list Tinder. In the name of testing, I went all in on Duet and gave it everything: my work email, calendar, Google Docs, and Slack. This gave it plenty of grist for the mill in more ways than I’d even realized at first. Because our biweekly staff meeting is automatically summarized in an email from Gemini, and Duet had access to my email, it was able to connect the dots between something said in a meeting and a direct message in Slack. Duet also worked out who my boss is because we have a shared Google Doc for our weekly 1:1 meetings. AI is at its most useful when it can suck up lots of data, and Duet wasted no time doing so. summary.tldr: Anthropic has released Claude Duet, a consumer-focused AI agent designed for professionals and small business owners. Unlike previous Anthropic offerings like Claude Code or Claude Cowork, Duet is specifically engineered to integrate with productivity suites—including email, calendars, Google Docs, and Slack—to proactively manage workflows, summarize meeting action items, and identify discrepancies across communication channels.
takeaways: **Integration Capabilities:** Duet functions by ingesting data from connected services (email, calendar, Google Docs, Slack) to generate "cards" that users can swipe to accept or hide, functioning as an automated task manager.

**Proactive Workflow Management:** The agent provides daily morning briefings and identifies potential scheduling conflicts or missed deadlines by cross-referencing disparate data sources, such as linking meeting summaries in email to Slack messages.

**Platform Availability:** The service is delivered via a dedicated mobile app that supports the iPhone Duo and is restricted to Anthropic's higher-tier subscription plans (Pro, Max, and Ultra) in the US.

**Transparency Features:** AI-generated communications sent via the agent, such as Slack messages, are automatically tagged with a "sent with Claude" label to ensure transparency in professional correspondence.

**Current Limitations:** The agent is currently undergoing testing regarding its "judgment" on notification frequency and tone, as it has demonstrated difficulty in distinguishing between hard deadlines and flexible project timelines.

title: JFinBench: A Continuously Refreshable Japanese Financial Benchmark from the Latest Certification Exams
author: Issa Sugiura
contentSnippet: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly applied to finance, creating a need for benchmarks that evaluate their capabilities across financial systems with different regulations and practices. However, existing financial benchmarks provide limited coverage of country-specific financial systems, and they are difficult to keep up to date as released questions leak into training data. We introduce JFinBench, a Japanese financial benchmark comprising 321 examples from the 2026 editions of six regularly administered certification exams covering accounting, tax, financial planning, and banking. To construct it, we develop a human-in-the-loop agentic pipeline in which a coding agent writes exam-specific conversion code and a review page, while a human verifies every example and feeds corrections back to the agent. This pipeline adapts to heterogeneous exam formats and reduces the effort of incorporating new exam editions, enabling periodic refreshes that mitigate data contamination. Evaluating 12 recent LLMs, we find that Claude Fable 5 and GPT-6 Astra exceed 93% overall, while even the best open-weight model, Kimi K3.1 Pro, trails Claude Fable 5 by 12 percentage points. When models can additionally use a terminal and web access, they retrieve the knowledge they lack and every model improves. The gap narrows but about 4 points remain, and the ranking of models stays largely the same, suggesting that knowledge held in the model itself remains valuable even with tools. We release the dataset, the evaluation code, and the construction pipeline.

title: Israel’s VCs see opportunity for challengers in Nvidia’s turmoil
author: Anna Heim
contentSnippet:
Former Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s resignation has been received with worry in Israel, the company’s “second home,” as Huang described it in 2023. The company’s importance flows both ways, as the semiconductor giant has provided a major boost to Israel’s economic forecasts in recent years.

Intel, Microsoft and many homegrown startups also conduct a sizable share of their R&D in Israel. But owing to Nvidia’s stronghold on AI given the centrality of its GPUs for training LLMs and using them, many in the country are wondering how much of a reshuffle will result from its leadership crisis.

As with everything at Nvidia, Huang drove the company to acquire Israeli chipmaker Mellanox for $6.9 billion in 2019 and use the company as the base for its largest R&D facility outside of the U.S. Nvidia also made plans to build a multibillion-dollar campus in northern Israel.

“Jensen brought Nvidia to Israel with the acquisition of Mellanox, so there is a strong positive sentiment towards Nvidia and Jensen in Israel’s tech community,” Israeli repeat cybersecurity entrepreneur Pavel Gurvich told TechCrunch.

Beyond the 6,000 locals Nvidia employs, the bigger question is whether the company will remain as committed to Israel with someone else at the helm. As a result, his line of succession is being observed just as closely by those who hope the company continues to do so as by those who don’t want it to happen.

The latter have already gathered that they may be in for disappointment. In a 2023 interview that is now doing the rounds on X, interim CEO Colette Kress had declared that as Nvidia’s CFO, she typically started her day “with Israel meetings, and only then continue[d] to California.”

Kress may not remain in charge in the long run, but the many names floated for the role include two Israelis , Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan — although they’re not at the top of the still quite tentative list .

Regardless of who gets chosen, Huang’s successor will likely have less of a grip on Nvidia and the tech industry as a whole. But investors don’t think that would cause demand for Nvidia’s product to fade away.

According to Yanai Oron, a general partner at Vertex Ventures Israel, “slower decisions at Nvidia could give competitors an opening, but if that uncertainty also slows AI spending, they could end up with a bigger share of a smaller opportunity.”

Nvidia h

summary.tldr:
Nvidia is facing a leadership transition following the resignation of CEO Jensen Huang, creating significant uncertainty within Israel’s technology sector, where the company maintains its largest R&D presence outside the U.S. Nvidia employs approximately 6,000 people in Israel, a footprint established largely through the $6.9 billion acquisition of Mellanox in 2019. The Israeli tech community, which views Nvidia as a critical economic pillar, is closely monitoring the succession process to determine if the company’s commitment to local R&D and planned multibillion-dollar campus infrastructure will persist under new leadership.

Industry analysts and venture capitalists suggest that while Nvidia’s core technology and ecosystem remain robust, the leadership vacuum may provide a strategic opening for competitors. Yanai Oron of Vertex Ventures Israel notes that while slower decision-making at Nvidia could benefit rivals, it risks cooling overall AI spending, potentially shrinking the total addressable market. Investors like Adi Levanon of Selah Ventures argue that while the company is unlikely to collapse, the transition may prevent Nvidia from achieving a total monopoly, allowing challengers in AI-specific chips and inference software to compete on economic efficiency and alternative architectural approaches.
takeaways: **Israel Footprint:** Nvidia employs 6,000 people in Israel and operates its largest R&D facility outside the U.S., a legacy of the 2019 Mellanox acquisition.
**Succession Candidates:** Potential candidates for the CEO role include Apple’s Johny Srouji and Nvidia’s Michael Kagan, though neither is currently considered a frontrunner.
**Interim Leadership:** Nvidia CFO Colette Kress is currently serving as interim CEO, having previously managed daily operations with a heavy focus on Israeli R&D coordination.
**Market Impact:** Analysts suggest that leadership uncertainty may allow competitors to gain market share in AI-specific hardware and inference software by offering better unit economics.

title: Contagious Fingerprints: When LLMs Inherit Another Model's Identity
author: Zailong Tian
contentSnippet: The fingerprint by which a classifier recognizes the LLM behind a text is usually treated as a fixed property of the model. We show that it is contagious: a model that continues a conversation begun by another model inherits that model's fingerprint. This undermines audits of API relays, which can serve the first turns of a conversation with the model a customer pays for and silently hand the rest to a cheaper one. After such a handoff, detection of the substitute by a text classifier drops from 0.97 to 0.72 (DeepSeek replacing Claude Sonnet) and from 0.87 to 0.54 for a same-vendor downgrade (Haiku), and retraining on handoff data repairs only substitutes seen in training. Preregistered experiments trace the contagion to imitation of the history's style. History also moves a model away from its own fingerprint: active probes are not camouflaged, but when calibrated on fresh conversations they flag \emph{honest} models on long contexts at rates up to 1.00, and a standard MMD equality test rejects all nine models we test. Both failures come from comparing a history-dependent reply with a history-free reference. We propose \textsc{Lineup}, which samples references from the claimed model \emph{on the same history} and tests the audited reply by its rank among them. \textsc{Lineup} controls false positives by exchangeability and needs no fitted threshold or log-probabilities. With contemporaneous references on two closed models, its false-positive rate is 0.056 (preregistered bound 0.10), and it detects 0.81 of substitute sessions across six pairs after four audited turns.

title: Jensen Huang didn’t show confidence in his successor, report says
author: Ivan Mehta
contentSnippet: Former NVIDIA CEO Jensen Huang described Colette Kress, the company’s CFO who has now replaced him as interim CEO, as “a deer in the headlights” during a presentation earlier in the summer, the Wall Street Journal reported , citing an anonymous source. Huang made the comment during a meeting with Nvidia’s finance team about the company’s plans to provide guarantees worth billions of dollars to data center operators that couldn’t afford to buy its chips upfront, according to the report. He reportedly also said Kress was a person who couldn’t help him steer strategy or decision-making. Kress has been with Nvidia for over 13 years now, after serving as SVP and CFO of Cisco’s Business Technology Operations Finance. The report said she has questioned Nvidia’s program-focused, credit-based deals involving Huang’s son-in-law Nico Caprez, and wanted to know how to decide which deals are beneficial, how to value guarantees, and determine returns. Earlier in the year, she had scaled back on Nvidia’s commitment for OpenAI’s ambitious Ohio data center project. The company was in talks to provide $250 billion in credit to OpenAI, but ended up committing $105 billion . Huang resigned Thursday after reports of two extramarital affairs , including one with the company’s VP for healthcare, Kimberly Powell. The company is also investigating a possible Chinese espionage plot . After his resignation, Reuters reported that he was having a third affair with another employee . Nvidia is currently searching for a permanent CEO to replace Huang, who had the top job for over 33 years. summary.tldr:
Nvidia CFO Colette Kress has assumed the role of interim CEO following the resignation of Jensen Huang, who stepped down after 33 years of leadership. Huang’s departure follows reports of multiple extramarital affairs, including one with Nvidia’s VP for healthcare, Kimberly Powell, and another with an unnamed employee. The company is currently conducting a search for a permanent successor while simultaneously investigating a potential Chinese espionage plot.

Internal friction preceded the leadership transition, with reports indicating that Huang held a low opinion of Kress’s strategic capabilities. During a summer meeting regarding Nvidia’s credit-based data center financing programs, Huang reportedly described Kress as a "deer in the headlights" and stated she was unable to assist in high-level decision-making. Kress, a 13-year Nvidia veteran and former Cisco executive, had previously challenged the company’s credit-heavy deal structures—which involved Huang’s son-in-law, Nico Caprez—and questioned the valuation and return metrics of these guarantees. Notably, Kress had previously reduced Nvidia’s credit commitment to OpenAI’s Ohio data center project from a proposed $250 billion to $105 billion.

title: Google Releases TPU Sync: Open-Source KV Cache Transfer for TPUs
author: Michal Sutter
contentSnippet: Google Cloud has released TPU Sync , an open-source C++ library for moving KV caches and model weights on Cloud TPUs. The Google TPU Sync KV cache transfer library treats TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage and the data center network as one memory hierarchy. It targets a growing bottleneck: moving model state, not computing it. Google reports over 90% lower KV transfer latency on 235B to 480B parameter MoE models. TL;DR Library: Native C++ core with Python wheels for PyTorch and JAX. Tested on 235B to 480B MoE models. Runs on: Cloud TPU v7x (Ironwood) and v6e per the README . Benchmarks used TPU v7x (2x2x1), PCIe Gen5 and 200 Gbps NICs. Performance: Large cuts to KV transfer latency and time to first token (TTFT) in Google’s internal lab tests. Best: Up to 90% lower average TTFT (480B P/D serving at low concurrency, and 64K-context prefix caching). Worst: No RL numbers published. The README says it is not yet recommended for general use. Bottom line: Best: Qwen3 235B KV transfer drops from several seconds to ~230 ms. Worst: every number is self-reported and early-stage. What is TPU Sync? TPU Sync is an open-source C++ library from Google that moves TPU-tiled tensors across memory tiers with asynchronous DMA. It handles 2 jobs: KV cache state during inference, and trainer-to-sampler weight broadcast in reinforcement learning (RL). The repository is licensed Apache-2.0. How does TPU Sync work? The library spans TPU HBM, pinned host DRAM, shared storage and multi-host DCN. Storage uses experimental POSIX backends, including local SSDs and Google Cloud Managed Lustre. Google lists 4 design choices: Layout-preserving direct DMA: It reads JAX PJRT buffers or PyTorch tensors in place. Data keeps its native TPU tile layout, with no Python serialization or bounce buffers. Compute-overlapped transfers: Raw PJRT buffer aliases let transfers run during computation. Built-in DMA pacing stops large copies from delaying kernel launches. No XLA compilation in the data path: Transfers and resharding run in native C++ outside the XLA graph. High-bandwidth PCIe and DCN: It reaches up to 223 GB/s per Ironwood host, against a 256 GB/s PCIe Gen5 ceiling. DCN streaming hits ~192 Gbps on 1 NIC, or ~350 Gbps across 2. Above this sit a global KV store for prefix lookups, a transfer controller and a KV cache manager. How does disaggregated prefill/decode serving use it? The prefill no

summary.tldr:
Google Cloud has open-sourced TPU Sync, a C++ library designed to optimize the movement of KV caches and model weights across Cloud TPU memory hierarchies. By treating TPU HBM, host DRAM, shared storage, and data center networks as a unified memory space, the library aims to mitigate bottlenecks in large-scale model inference. It supports PyTorch and JAX via Python wheels and is specifically engineered for massive Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models, with testing conducted on 235B to 480B parameter architectures on TPU v7x (Ironwood) and v6e hardware.

Technically, TPU Sync utilizes asynchronous DMA to move TPU-tiled tensors without Python serialization or bounce buffers, preserving native layouts to avoid XLA compilation overhead. The library achieves up to 90% reduction in average Time to First Token (TTFT) for 480B parameter models at low concurrency with 64K-context prefix caching. In specific benchmarks, Qwen3 235B KV transfer latency dropped from several seconds to approximately 230 ms. The architecture leverages PCIe Gen5 and 200 Gbps NICs, reaching throughputs of 223 GB/s per host and up to 350 Gbps across dual-NIC DCN configurations.

While the library is available under an Apache-2.0 license, Google explicitly notes it is not yet recommended for general production use. The system integrates with experimental POSIX backends, including local SSDs and Google Cloud Managed Lustre, to manage state across multi-host environments. Despite the performance gains, the current documentation lacks reinforcement learning (RL) benchmarks, and all reported metrics are internal, early-stage results.
takeaways: **Performance Gains:** Achieves up to 90% lower average TTFT for 480B MoE models and reduces Qwen3 235B KV transfer latency to ~230 ms.
**Hardware Throughput:** Reaches 223 GB/s per Ironwood host (near the 256 GB/s PCIe Gen5 ceiling) and up to 350 Gbps across two 200 Gbps NICs.
**Architectural Design:** Operates outside the XLA graph using native C++ to perform layout-preserving direct DMA, avoiding Python serialization and bounce buffers.
**Supported Environments:** Compatible with TPU v7x (Ironwood) and v6e, utilizing experimental POSIX backends like local SSDs and Google Cloud Managed Lustre.
**Integration:** Provides Python wheels for PyTorch and JAX, treating TPU HBM, host DRAM, and DCN as a unified memory hierarchy.

title: WebArena-Pro: A Heterogeneous, Multimodal, Reproducible Benchmark for Web Agents
author: Imene Kerboua
contentSnippet: Web agents powered by large language and vision-language models are increasingly applied to realistic browser work that spans heterogeneous applications, multimodal content, and stateful workflows. However, existing reproducible web-agent benchmarks cover only a small number of web applications drawn from a few software categories, and restrict modality to text and vision. Live benchmarks broaden site coverage but sacrifice reproducibility, since pages and data drift between runs. Moreover, existing benchmarks do not meaningfully evaluate whether agents can understand and use audio and video content embedded within web tasks. To address these gaps, we introduce WebArena-Pro, a benchmark comprising 300 tasks across 20 self-hosted web applications in six domain categories, spanning distinct interface conventions, workflows, and data models. Across the evaluated agents, the best performance is achieved by both Codex with GPT 6.1 Sol and Claude Code with Claude Opus 5.5 at 62.3%, followed by OpenCode with Kimi 3.1 Pro at 60.7%. The strongest GenericAgent configurations, Gemini 3.1 Pro omni and Gemma4 31B, both achieve 30.3%. Among reproducible, human-curated web agent benchmarks, WebArena-Pro provides the broadest application coverage and the most comprehensive multimodal support to date. The benchmark treats audio and video as core observations alongside text and vision, with dedicated actions for extracting information from each. WebArena-Pro runs each task in isolation and supports reproducible, parallel evaluation. Tasks are authored through a dedicated annotator interface, filtered by LLM-assisted triage, and finally validated by humans before release. Project page: https://webarena-pro.github.io

title: UltraBERT-JEV: Encoder models for System One Applications
author: Astarag Mohapatra
contentSnippet: We study encoder models that pick one of several options in a single forward pass, without generating text. This technical report compares recipes for fine-tuning UltraBERT-380M with one mask per option. The four recipes differ in how an option is scored and how the scores become probabilities; one follows the expert gate of DeepSeek-V3. Trained on the same data as Qwen3-0.6B with the LLM-as-Jev recipe (67.6% test accuracy), the encoder reaches 69.7% to 72.1%. Scoring an option by "yes" minus "no" instead of "yes" alone gives the larger gain, from 69.7% to 71.3% on the test set and from 57.8% to 59.6% on external benchmarks (56.1% for the decoder). Sigmoid normalisation adds 0.8 test points; a square-root softplus adds none. One request at a time on an NVIDIA A100, the encoder takes 29 ms per decision against 68 ms, but uses more peak memory (2.8 against 2.2 GiB). An auxiliary head, trained on human-marked evidence and on labels selected with a reward adapted from SelfCite, predicts in the same pass the sentences annotated as support for the answer.

title: Is Abliteration Getting Harder? Not Uniformly: Refusal Removal by Direction-Based Ablation and ARA in Heretic on the Qwen3.8, Gemma 4, Olmo 3.1 and Mistral Small 3.2 LLMs Versus Their Predecessors
author: Richard J. Young
contentSnippet: Abliteration, a fine-tuning-free weight edit, removes refusal from open-weight large language models (LLMs). The developer of Arbitrary-Rank Ablation (ARA), an optimisation-based variant, reports that direction-based abliteration, which ablates a refusal direction, increasingly fails on newer models. On five release pairs, refusal removal did not become uniformly harder. Qwen2.5-32B and Qwen3.8-27B, Gemma-2-27B and Gemma-4-31B, OLMo-2-32B and Olmo-3.1-32B, Mistral-Small-2409 and Mistral-Small-3.2, and Qwen2.5-7B and Qwen3.5-4B were edited in Heretic 2.0 by three or four direction-based methods (difference-in-means, MPOA, SOM and, on the small pair, J-space) and ARA under the same prompts, nominal search budget, first-token KL divergence cap and selection rule; removal counted as harder when the automatic WildGuard judge found more of 972 held-out harmful prompts (JailbreakBench, XSTest, StrongREJECT, HarmBench and an author-compiled malicious-code bank) still refused. After direction-based removal, newer releases retained -1 to +37 percentage points more refusal, and after ARA -26 to +34. With run-to-run variance included, between-pair heterogeneity of the direction-based effect ranged from high to low with the scale and variance model (I^2 20-80%). ARA lost less effectiveness than direction-based methods in Gemma and OLMo and more in Qwen; each verdict rests on one ARA run, and some changed with the divergence budget or variance model. In Gemma the direction-based increase came from the malicious-code bank and reversed on public sets. Contrary to prediction, keyword counts at the tool's window did not undercount judged refusal on average, but differed by a mean 7 points per model. Audits of a single pair, method or prompt source can reach opposite conclusions. Whether a newer model resisted removal depended on the release pair, method and budget, not on generation alone.
